docs.title: Userli
docs.text:
Userli is a free and open-source web application to (self-) manage email accounts and encrypt their mailboxes. It is developed by systemli.org, a non-profit tech collective that runs it for its own email service, and released under the AGPL v3.

Userli is the user database and self-service portal of a mail server. It does not send or store emails itself. Instead, Dovecot and Postfix ask Userli who is allowed to log in, which addresses exist and where mail has to go.

docs.title: Who is this documentation for?
docs.text:
• Users

    You have (or want) an email account on a server that runs Userli. Learn how to register, sign in, protect your account and manage aliases.

    User Guide

  • Admins and domain admins

    You manage the accounts of a mail service or of a single domain. Learn how to manage users, aliases, invite codes, domains and settings.

    Admin Guide

  • Server operators

    You install and operate Userli and connect it to Postfix, Dovecot and other services.

    Operations

  • Developers

    You want to fix a bug, build a feature, translate or improve these docs.

    Development

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
For users

  • Registration with invite codes – existing users invite new users
  • Self-service: change password, create aliases, delete the account
  • Custom and random alias addresses
  • Two-factor authentication (TOTP) with backup codes
  • Recovery token to regain access after losing the password
  • Publishing OpenPGP keys via Web Key Directory
  • Available in English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, Bokmål and Swiss German

For admins

  • Web interface for users, aliases, domains, invite codes, reserved names, settings, API tokens and webhooks
  • Multiple domains with domain admins who only see their own domain
  • Roles to mark accounts as spam or suspicious, or to protect them from the removal of inactive accounts
  • Automatic maintenance: removal of inactive accounts, cleanup of old data, weekly registration report

For operators

  • Mailbox encryption with Dovecot MailCrypt – keys are protected with the user's password
  • HTTP APIs for Dovecot, Postfix, Roundcube, Keycloak and more, secured with scoped API tokens
  • Webhooks to keep other services in sync
  • MTA-STS policy hosting
  • Prometheus metrics

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    U[Users and admins<br/>web browser] -->|HTTPS| W[Userli]
    D[Dovecot<br/>IMAP / POP3] -->|auth and mailbox lookup<br/>incl. MailCrypt keys| W
    P[Postfix<br/>SMTP] -->|domains, mailboxes,<br/>aliases, SASL auth| W
    R[Roundcube] -->|alias lookup| W
    K[Keycloak] -->|user lookup and<br/>credential check| W
    W -->|webhooks| X[Other services<br/>Nextcloud, Matrix, ...]
    W --- DB[(MariaDB / MySQL)]

Userli is a Symfony application written in PHP. It stores its data in MariaDB or MySQL and uses a background worker for emails, webhooks and recurring maintenance tasks.

docs.title: Get involved
docs.text:
Userli is free software and contributions are very welcome: code, translations, bug reports and documentation.

  • Source code and issues: github.com/systemli/userli
  • Good first issues: issue tracker
  • Start here: Development

Everyone involved is expected to follow our Code of Conduct.

docs.title: Admin Guide
docs.text: This guide is for people who manage the email accounts of a Userli installation – either for all domains (admins) or for a single domain (domain admins). It explains the admin interface. Installing and operating the server is covered in Operations.

docs.title: Open the admin interface
docs.text:
Sign in with an admin account and click Admin in the navigation bar, or open /admin/ directly.

The sidebar groups all pages:

Group Pages Admin Domain admin Management Dashboard, Users, Aliases, Invite Codes, App Passwords, OpenPGP Keys ✓ ✓ (own domain) Domain settings (own domain) ✓ Configuration Domains, Reserved Names, Notifications ✓ System Settings, API Tokens, Webhooks, Maintenance ✓

Try it out

The screenshots in this guide were taken with the example data from make fixtures. See the development setup to run your own test instance.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text: The dashboard shows the number of users, new users and active users in the last 7 and 30 days, aliases and published OpenPGP keys. Admins also see the number of domains and redeemed and unused invite codes. Domain admins only see numbers for their own domain.

docs.title: OpenPGP keys
docs.text: Management → OpenPGP Keys is a read-only list of all keys that users have published in the Web Key Directory. Use the search to find keys by email address or domain. Users manage their keys themselves, see OpenPGP keys in the User Guide.

docs.title: App passwords
docs.text: Management → App Passwords is a read-only list of the app passwords users have generated, with name and last use (rounded to the start of the week, like the last login of users). Use the search to find them by email address or domain. Users manage their app passwords themselves, see App passwords in the User Guide.

docs.title: Common tasks
docs.text: Task How Create an account for someone Users → Create A user lost password and recovery token Set a new password (encrypted mails are lost) Account sends spam Add the role Spam Account invited spammers Add the role Suspicious Delete a custom alias for a user Aliases → Delete Give someone unlimited invite codes Add the role Multiplier Open registration for a domain Domains → Edit → Invitations Restore a deleted account Users → Restore

docs.title: Aliases
docs.text:
Management → Aliases lists the aliases of all users. Domain admins only see the aliases of their own domain.

An alias forwards emails from a source address to a destination address. Users create aliases themselves (see Aliases in the User Guide):

  • up to 3 custom aliases, which they can't delete themselves,
  • up to 100 random aliases, which they can delete at any time.

Filter the list by domain and status (active or deleted).

docs.title: Create and edit aliases
docs.text:
Admins can create aliases with any source on a managed domain and

  • assign them to a user – emails go to that user, or
  • set a free destination address – for example to forward to an external mailbox or a mailing list,
  • set SMTP quota limits for the alias.

Domain admins can create aliases in their own domain and assign them to a user. They can't set a free destination or quotas.

Warning

When a domain admin saves an alias with a free destination, the destination is replaced by the assigned user. Ask an admin to edit such aliases.

docs.title: Delete aliases
docs.text:
Delete aliases with the delete action, for example when a user asks to remove a custom alias. A deleted address is blocked and can't be registered or used as an alias again.

The CLI command bin/console app:alias:delete does the same, see Console commands.

docs.title: postmaster@ and abuse@
docs.text: postmaster@ and abuse@ addresses for all domains are configured globally under Settings → RFC Email Addresses. If set, they take precedence over aliases with the same address.

docs.title: API tokens
docs.text: System → API Tokens (admins only) manages the tokens that other services – Dovecot, Postfix, Roundcube, Keycloak – use to talk to Userli.

docs.title: Create a token
docs.text:
Click Create, enter a descriptive name (for example Dovecot mx1) and select one or more scopes:

Scope Used by dovecot Dovecot – login and mailbox lookups postfix Postfix – domains, mailboxes, aliases, SMTP auth roundcube Roundcube – alias lookup keycloak Keycloak – single sign-on retention Retention – activity of external services

Copy the token immediately

The token is shown only once after creation. Userli only stores a hash. Hand it to your server operator through a secure channel.

docs.title: Good practice
docs.text:
• Create one token per service and server, with only the scopes it needs.
  • The list shows when each token was last used. Delete unused tokens.
  • If a token leaked, delete it and create a new one.

docs.title: Domains
docs.text: Configuration → Domains lists the email domains managed by Userli. Only admins can add and delete domains.

docs.title: Add a domain
docs.text:
Click Create and enter the domain name, for example example.org.

Userli only manages the accounts. Before users can receive mail on a new domain, your server operator has to configure DNS (MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, optionally MTA-STS) and the mail server for it.

docs.title: Default domain
docs.text:
The first domain you created (lowest ID) is the default domain:

  • Users of this domain can sign in with only the part before the @.
  • bin/console app:admin:password sets the password of postmaster@<default domain>.

docs.title: Domain details
docs.text: The detail page shows the number of users, aliases, domain admins and invite codes of the domain.

docs.title: Invitations
docs.text:
Registration in Userli works only with invite codes. Invitations are configured per domain under Edit:

Setting Description Enabled Allow registration with invite codes for this domain. If disabled, visitors with a code see "Registration closed". Existing accounts are not affected. Limit Number of invite codes each user receives automatically. 0 means users don't get codes, but multipliers and admins can still create them. Waiting period Days after registration before users receive their codes (default 7).

New domains have invitations disabled.

docs.title: Domain admins
docs.text:
Domain admins manage the users, aliases and invite codes of their own domain and can edit its invitation settings via Management → Domain settings.

To make someone domain admin, give their account the role Domain admin. The account must belong to the domain. See Roles and permissions.

docs.title: Delete a domain
docs.text:
Deletes all data of the domain

Deleting a domain permanently deletes all users, aliases, invite codes and OpenPGP keys of that domain. Unlike deleting a single user, this is a hard delete: the addresses become available again, and no user.deleted webhooks are sent.

Click delete and confirm with your password. You can't delete the domain of your own account. Webhooks that were limited to only this domain are disabled.

On the command line, use bin/console app:domain:delete --domain example.org --dry-run to see what would be deleted first.

docs.title: Invite codes
docs.text:
New accounts can only be registered with an invite code (also called voucher). Each code belongs to a user and a domain and can be used once. The new account is created in the domain of the code.

Management → Invite Codes lists all codes with owner, domain and whether they were redeemed.

docs.title: How users get invite codes
docs.text:
Users get codes automatically when they open their invite code page and

  • invitations are enabled for their domain,
  • their account is older than the domain's waiting period,
  • they have signed in at least once,
  • they have fewer codes than the domain's limit (redeemed codes count, so the limit is a lifetime total),
  • they don't have the role Suspicious.

Users with the role Multiplier (including domain admins and admins) can create codes on their invite code page at any time. See Roles and permissions.

docs.title: Create invite codes
docs.text:
Click Create, choose the owner and – as admin – the domain. Admins can create codes for any domain; domain admins only for their own domain, and only if invitations are enabled for it. The limit per user doesn't apply.

To create several codes at once and print registration links, use the command line:

bin/console app:voucher:create --user admin@example.org --count 10 --print-links

docs.title: Delete invite codes
docs.text: Delete unused codes with the delete action, for example when they were shared publicly.

docs.title: Automatic cleanup
docs.text:
• Unused codes of deleted users are removed.
  • Three months after a code was redeemed, the link between the code and the new account is removed for privacy. After that, you can no longer see who invited whom.

See Maintenance.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:
Userli runs maintenance tasks automatically in the background. Under System → Maintenance (admins only) you can start them manually, for example after changing data or when the scheduler is not running.

Task Schedule What it does Prune webhook deliveries daily, 03:00 Removes successful webhook deliveries older than 14 days. Failed ones are kept. Prune user notifications daily, 03:30 Removes notifications older than 30 days. Unlink redeemed invite codes daily, 04:00 Removes the link between an invite code and the account that used it, three months after registration. Remove unredeemed invite codes weekly, 05:00 Removes unused invite codes of deleted users. Remove inactive users weekly, 06:00 Deletes accounts without sign-in for more than two years (737 days). Accounts with role Admin, Domain admin or Permanent are skipped. Weekly report weekly, 07:00 Emails the registrations of the last 7 days to the notification address, if enabled. Can't be started manually.

Times are server time. Manually started tasks run in the background within a few seconds.

Inactive users

Every sign-in counts – web interface, IMAP/POP3 via Dovecot, SMTP via Postfix or Keycloak. Services that keep users logged in for a long time should report activity via the Retention API, otherwise their users may be removed.

Note

The tasks only run automatically if the worker and scheduler processes are running, see Background services.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text: Configuration → Notifications (admins only) is a log of security notices that Userli has shown to users. Filter by type or search by email address.

docs.title: Compromised passwords
docs.text:
Currently there is one type: password compromised.

Every time a user signs in – on the web or via the mail server – Userli checks the password against the Have I Been Pwned database, at most once every 7 days per user. Only the first characters of a hash of the password are sent, never the password itself (k-anonymity).

If the password was found:

  • a notification is stored and listed here,
  • the user sees a red Security Alert banner in the web interface until they change their password,
  • the user detail page shows a warning.

No email is sent to the user.

Notifications are removed when the user changes the password, when the account is deleted, and automatically after 30 days (see Maintenance).

docs.title: Reserved names
docs.text:
Configuration → Reserved Names (admins only) lists names that can't be registered or used as alias, for example admin, abuse, postmaster or support. A reserved name blocks the part before the @ on all domains.

  • Create adds a single name.
  • Delete removes a name.
  • Import adds names from a text file.
  • Export downloads all names as reserved_names.txt.

docs.title: Import format
docs.text:
A plain text file (up to 1 MB) with one name per line. Empty lines and lines starting with # are ignored, names are converted to lowercase, and existing names are skipped.

# Common role addresses
admin
hostmaster
webmaster

A curated list of about 570 common names is available at contrib/reserved_names.txt. Import it right after the initial setup.

Reserved names don't affect existing accounts or aliases.

docs.title: Roles and permissions
docs.text:
Every account has one or more roles. Roles are set by admins when creating or editing a user.

Role (in the UI) Technical name Effect User ROLE_USER Default role of every account. Admin ROLE_ADMIN Full access to the admin interface, all domains and all settings. Domain admin ROLE_DOMAIN_ADMIN Manages users, aliases and invite codes of their own domain. Includes Permanent and Multiplier. Permanent ROLE_PERMANENT The account is never removed as inactive. Multiplier ROLE_MULTIPLIER Can create invite codes at any time, without limit and waiting period. Suspicious ROLE_SUSPICIOUS No invite codes; already issued codes of this user become invalid. Spam ROLE_SPAM Account is locked: no sending, no IMAP/POP3 login. Includes Suspicious.

docs.title: Spam
docs.text:
Use Spam when an account is compromised or sends spam.

  • SMTP authentication (Postfix) and IMAP/POP3 login (Dovecot) are refused. The user can't send or read emails anymore.
  • Incoming emails are still delivered to the mailbox.
  • The user can still sign in to the web interface but only sees an "Account locked" page with a request to contact support. Aliases and OpenPGP keys can't be managed.
  • All effects of Suspicious apply, too.

To unlock the account, remove the role. Consider requiring a password change at the same time.

docs.title: Suspicious
docs.text:
Use Suspicious when an account invites spammers or abusers.

  • The user doesn't get invite codes anymore and the invite code page is hidden.
  • Unused invite codes of this user can't be used for registration anymore.
  • When the role is added, Userli emails a list of all accounts that registered with this user's invite codes to the notification address (see Settings). Review them, too.

Accounts with Suspicious or Spam are marked in the user search.

docs.title: Multiplier
docs.text: Multipliers see a Create invite code button on their invite code page and can create as many codes as they want – as long as invitations are enabled for their domain. Use this for people who onboard many users, for example the organizers of a group.

docs.title: Permanent
docs.text: Userli regularly removes accounts that were not used for about two years (see Maintenance). Accounts with Permanent, Domain admin or Admin are skipped. Use it for role or function accounts that nobody signs in to.

docs.title: Admins and domain admins
docs.text:
Admin Domain admin Users, aliases, invite codes, OpenPGP keys all domains own domain Manage users with role Admin ✓ Assignable roles all User, Domain admin, Permanent Set alias destination and SMTP quota ✓ Edit invitation settings of a domain all domains own domain Create and delete domains ✓ Reserved names, notifications ✓ Settings, API tokens, webhooks, maintenance ✓

The domain of a domain admin is the domain of their own email address.

Domain admins and restricted roles

Domain admins can't assign Spam, Suspicious or Multiplier. When a domain admin saves a user who has one of these roles, the role may be removed. Ask an admin to edit such accounts.

docs.title: The first admin
docs.text:
The setup wizard creates the first admin account postmaster@<domain>, see Initial setup. You can (re)set its password on the command line:

bin/console app:admin:password

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: System → Settings (admins only) contains the global settings of the installation. They are stored in the database and apply immediately. The basic settings are first set in the setup wizard.

docs.title: Application settings
docs.text: Setting Default Description App name Userli Name in the header, browser title and start page (3–30 characters). App URL https://users.example.org Public URL of Userli. Used in links in emails and invite links. Webmail URL – URL of your webmail. Shows a Webmail card to users. Leave empty to hide it.

docs.title: Project settings
docs.text: Setting Default Description Project name example.org Name of your project or organization, used on the welcome page and in emails. Project URL https://www.example.org Website of your project.

docs.title: Email configuration
docs.text: Setting Default Description Sender address admin@example.org Sender of all emails from Userli. Notification address monitoring@example.org Receives the weekly report and reports about suspicious users.

docs.title: Mailbox encryption
docs.text:
Setting Default Description MailCrypt 2 0 disabled, 1 optional, 2 enforce for new users, 3 enforce for all users.

See MailCrypt for what the levels mean and how to migrate existing users. Keep the default unless you know why to change it.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text: Setting Default Description Weekly report on Every week, send a list of new registrations to the notification address.

docs.title: SMTP quota limits
docs.text:
Setting Default Description Per hour 0 Default maximum number of emails a user can send per hour. 0 = unlimited. Per day 0 Default maximum number of emails a user can send per day. 0 = unlimited.

Limits can be overridden per user and per alias. Userli only provides the numbers – your mail server has to enforce them, see Postfix.

docs.title: MTA-STS
docs.text:
Setting Default Description Mode testing testing (report only), enforce (reject on failure) or none (opt out). MX hosts – Allowed MX hostnames, one per line, wildcards like *.example.org allowed. Max age 604800 How long (in seconds) sending servers cache the policy. 1 day to 1 year.

No policy is published while the MX list is empty. See MTA-STS for the required DNS records.

docs.title: RFC email addresses
docs.text:
Setting Default Description Postmaster address – Destination of postmaster@ on all domains (RFC 5321). Abuse address – Destination of abuse@ on all domains (RFC 2142).

If set, these override aliases with the same address. Leave empty to use aliases instead.

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
Management → Users lists all accounts. Domain admins only see the accounts of their own domain.

  • Search by email address.
  • Filter by status (active, deleted, all), role, MailCrypt, two-factor authentication and domain.
  • The list shows roles, whether 2FA and MailCrypt are enabled and whether the account is deleted.
  • Actions per row: show, edit, delete – or restore for deleted accounts.

docs.title: Show a user
docs.text: The detail page shows roles, status, MailCrypt and 2FA state, creation and last sign-in date, and the number of aliases, invite codes, redeemed invite codes, app passwords and OpenPGP keys. Click a card to see the matching list. It also warns if the user's password was found in a data breach recently.

docs.title: Create a user
docs.text:
Click Create and fill in:

Field Description Email Full address. The domain must exist. Domain admins can only use their own domain. Can't be changed later. Password At least 12 characters, not found in known data breaches. Roles See Roles and permissions. User is always added. Quota Optional mailbox size limit in MB. Passed to Dovecot. Empty means no limit. SMTP quota limits Optional maximum number of emails per hour and per day (admins only). Empty uses the global default. Password change required The user must choose a new password at the next sign-in. Always set for new users.

Users created in the admin interface:

  • must change the password before they can use email (web, IMAP, SMTP),
  • get mailbox encryption keys if MailCrypt is enforced (setting mail_crypt ≥ 2),
  • don't have a recovery token yet – ask them to create one,
  • don't receive a welcome email and don't trigger the user.created webhook.

Tip

For self-registration, create an invite code instead and send the user the registration link.

docs.title: Edit a user
docs.text:
The same fields as above, except the email address. Additionally:

  • Two-factor authentication: uncheck to turn off 2FA for a user who lost their phone and backup codes.

docs.title: Set a new password
docs.text:
Enter a password only if the user can't help themselves – they lost both their password and their recovery token.

Encrypted emails are lost

If the user has MailCrypt keys, setting a new password resets the account:

  • new MailCrypt keys are generated – all existing emails become unreadable,
  • a new recovery token is created and shown to you once – pass it on to the user securely,
  • two-factor authentication is turned off,
  • all app passwords are deleted,
  • the user.reset webhook is sent.

The user has to change the password at the next sign-in.

docs.title: Delete a user
docs.text:
Deleting is a soft delete. The account remains in the database so that the address can never be registered again, but:

  • the password is replaced by a random one, recovery token, MailCrypt keys and app passwords are erased,
  • all aliases of the user are deleted,
  • unused invite codes and notifications are removed,
  • the published OpenPGP key is removed,
  • the user.deleted webhook is sent.

The mailbox on the mail server is not deleted by Userli. Your server operator can do this with the mailbox janitor.

docs.title: Restore a user
docs.text:
Filter by status deleted and click restore on a deleted account. Set a new password. Userli

  • reactivates the account,
  • creates new MailCrypt keys and a new recovery token (shown once),
  • sends the welcome email.

Old encrypted emails can't be read anymore and aliases are not restored.

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text: System → Webhooks (admins only) configures URLs that Userli calls when accounts are created, deleted or reset. Webhooks keep other services – for example Nextcloud, Matrix or a script on the mail server – in sync with Userli.

docs.title: Create a webhook
docs.text:
Click Create and fill in:

Field Description URL Endpoint that receives the events. Secret Shared secret to sign the requests. The receiver needs the same secret. Events At least one of user.created, user.deleted, user.reset. Domains Optional. Only send events for users of these domains. Empty means all domains. Enabled Turn the webhook on or off. Event Sent when user.created A user registered with an invite code. user.deleted A user was deleted – by themselves, an admin or automatic cleanup. user.reset An admin set a new password for a user with mailbox encryption.

docs.title: Test and monitor
docs.text:
• Use the send action to send a test event.
  • Deliveries lists all calls of a webhook with status, response and number of attempts. Failed deliveries are retried automatically three times. You can retry a delivery manually after fixing the receiver.

Successful deliveries are removed after 14 days.

The payload format, signature and retry behaviour are described for developers of receivers in Operations → Webhooks.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
Userli is a Symfony-based web application for self-managing email users with mailbox encryption support (Dovecot). It is built with PHP, Symfony, Doctrine ORM, and uses TailwindCSS with Symfony UX on the frontend.

We provide a docker-compose.yml that starts Userli with MariaDB, Dovecot, Roundcube, Mailcatcher, Redis, and a webhook tester to set up a complete development environment.

Warning

This setup is meant for local development only. Do not use it in production. See the Operations Guide for production installations.

Service URL Purpose Userli http://localhost:8000 Main application Roundcube http://localhost:8001 Webmail client Mailcatcher http://localhost:1080 Catches all outgoing emails Webhook test http://localhost:9000 Webhook endpoint testing

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• podman (or docker) with compose support
  • yarn
  • composer
  • make

Info

If you don't have Podman or Docker installed, see the Podman or Docker installation instructions.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
For first-time setup, run:

make dev

This will:

  1. Install PHP dependencies and build frontend assets (make assets)
  2. Start all containers (MariaDB, Redis, Caddy, Userli, worker, scheduler, Mailcatcher, webhook tester)
  3. Wait for MariaDB to be ready
  4. Run database migrations

The Makefile auto-detects whether you have Podman or Docker installed.

docs.title: Load fixtures
docs.text:
To populate the environment with example data, run

make fixtures

This

  1. loads sample data (users, domains, API tokens, ...) and
  2. starts Dovecot and Roundcube (mail profile).

When it finishes, open http://localhost:8000 and log in with admin@example.org / password.

Info

The fixtures create user accounts (admin, user, support and suspicious, among others) on the domain example.org, all with the password password. They also create sample aliases and vouchers. See src/DataFixtures for details.

Info

Dovecot and Roundcube are in the mail profile and must be started after the fixtures are loaded in the database, otherwise Dovecot will fail because the API token it is configured to use will not exists in the database. make fixtures handles both in the right order.

Tip

Run make without arguments to see all available targets.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Get to know the code: Architecture
  • Read the contribution guidelines
  • Run the tests

  • Watch the frontend while you work:

    yarn watch

docs.title: Background services
docs.text:
The development environment runs three containers for the Userli application:

Container Purpose userli PHP-FPM, served by the caddy container userli-worker Async message consumer (messenger:consume async) userli-scheduler Scheduled tasks (messenger:consume scheduler_maintenance)

The worker processes async messages (e.g. email sending, webhook delivery). The scheduler runs recurring maintenance tasks defined in src/Schedule/.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
Userli uses Monolog for logging, configured in config/packages/monolog.yaml. Logs are JSON-formatted.

In development, logs are written to var/log/dev.log:

tail -f var/log/dev.log | jq

To inspect container logs:

podmandocker 
podman compose logs -f userli

docker compose logs -f userli

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
On systems with SELinux enabled, the webserver might throw an error due to broken filesystem permissions. Create a docker-compose.override.yml in the root directory:

---
services:
  userli:
    security_opt:
      - label=disable

  dovecot:
    security_opt:
      - label=disable

  roundcube:
    security_opt:
      - label=disable

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Userli is a Symfony 7.4 application written in PHP 8.4. It uses Doctrine ORM with MariaDB, Twig templates with Tailwind CSS and Stimulus controllers written in TypeScript, bundled with Webpack Encore.

The repository contains AGENTS.md files with detailed conventions per directory. They are written for AI coding assistants, but are a good reference for humans, too.

docs.title: Project structure
docs.text:
userli/
├── src/                    Application code
├── templates/              Twig templates
├── assets/                 Stimulus controllers, Tailwind CSS, TypeScript
├── config/                 Symfony configuration, routes, settings.yaml
├── migrations/             Doctrine migrations
├── default_translations/   Translations (EN/DE manual, others via Weblate)
├── tests/                  PHPUnit and Vitest tests, mirrors src/ and assets/
├── features/               Behat scenarios
├── contrib/                Dovecot Lua adapter, reserved names list
├── docker/                 Container images and configuration for development
└── docs/                   This documentation (MkDocs)

src/
├── Command/          Console commands (app:*)
├── Controller/       HTTP controllers
│   ├── Account/      User self-service
│   ├── Admin/        Admin interface
│   └── Api/          APIs for Dovecot, Postfix, Keycloak, Roundcube, Retention
├── DataFixtures/     Example data for development
├── Entity/           Doctrine entities (User, Domain, Alias, Voucher, …)
├── EntityListener/   Doctrine lifecycle listeners (cache invalidation, …)
├── Enum/             PHP enums (Roles, ApiScope, webhook events, cache keys, …)
├── Event/            Domain events
├── EventListener/    Symfony event listeners
├── Form/             Symfony form types
│   └── Model/        Form data models (never bind entities directly)
├── Handler/          Business logic (registration, MailCrypt, deletion, …)
├── Mail/             Mailers for user-facing emails
├── Message/          Messenger messages (async jobs)
├── MessageHandler/   Handlers for messages, 1:1 with Message/
├── Repository/       Doctrine repositories
├── Schedule/         Scheduler definition (maintenance tasks)
├── Security/         Authenticators, user provider, user checker
├── Service/          Business services (managers, webhook dispatcher, …)
├── Traits/           Entity composition traits
├── Twig/             Twig extensions and filters
├── Validator/        Custom constraints and validators
└── Voter/            Authorization voters

docs.title: Entities
docs.text: Entity Purpose User Email account with roles, password hash, 2FA, MailCrypt keys and recovery token. Composed of traits in src/Traits/. Domain Mail domain with embedded InvitationSettings. Alias Alias address, random or custom, pointing to a user or a destination. Voucher Invite code. ReservedName Blocked local parts. OpenPgpKey Published OpenPGP key for the Web Key Directory. ApiToken Hashed API token with scopes. WebhookEndpoint, WebhookDelivery Webhook configuration and delivery log. UserNotification Security notices for users. Setting Runtime settings, schema in config/settings.yaml.

docs.title: Domain scoping
docs.text: For every logged-in user who is not ROLE_ADMIN, a Doctrine SQL filter (src/Entity/Filter/DomainFilter.php) limits all queries on domain-aware entities to the user's own domain. This is how domain admins only see their domain. Voters (src/Voter/) add resource-level checks.

docs.title: Events, messages and the scheduler
docs.text:
• Domain events (src/Event/, e.g. UserEvent::USER_CREATED) are dispatched synchronously via the EventDispatcher and handled by listeners in src/EventListener/ – for example to send the welcome email or webhooks.
  • Messages (src/Message/) are processed asynchronously by the worker (messenger:consume async). Every message has exactly one handler in src/MessageHandler/. Messages are signed.
  • Scheduled tasks are defined in src/Schedule/MaintenanceSchedule.php. The scheduler dispatches messages that are then processed by the worker.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Settings that admins can change at runtime are defined in config/settings.yaml (type, default, validation, form options) and stored in the Setting entity. Read them in PHP via the settings service and in Twig with setting('name'). Environment variables are reserved for infrastructure configuration.

docs.title: Caching
docs.text: API lookups (Dovecot, Postfix, WKD, MTA-STS) are cached. Cache keys are defined as enums in src/Enum/*CacheKey.php. Entity listeners in src/EntityListener/ invalidate them on changes.

docs.title: MailCrypt
docs.text: src/Handler/MailCryptKeyHandler.php creates the key pairs (via openssl) and encrypts the private key with libsodium. See MailCrypt.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Controllers separate GET and POST into distinct methods with explicit methods in the #[Route] attribute. RegistrationController is the canonical example.
  • Forms never bind entities. Use models in src/Form/Model/.
  • Environment variables are injected with #[Autowire(env: 'VAR_NAME')].
  • Translations: all user-facing text uses the |trans filter, see Translations.
  • Security in templates: never use |raw for user-supplied data – use |safe_html. Never set innerHTML with unsanitized content.
  • No type error suppression (@psalm-suppress, @ts-ignore, as any).

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
Three base templates exist:

Template Use case Key blocks base.html.twig Root layout (dark mode, assets, navbar) — base_page.html.twig Full pages page_title, page_subtitle, page_content base_step.html.twig Multi-step flows (registration, recovery) step_icon, step_title, step_description, step_content, step_footer

Styling uses Tailwind CSS utility classes, with dark mode and mobile-first responsive layouts. Icons use Heroicons via Symfony UX Icons:

{{ ux_icon('heroicons:arrow-left', {class: 'size-5'}) }}

Stimulus controllers live in assets/controllers/ and are written in TypeScript.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Userli is free software and every contribution is welcome – code, bug reports, translations, documentation or ideas.

docs.title: Code of Conduct
docs.text: This project follows the Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct. Please read the full text before participating. For reports of abusive or unacceptable behavior, contact userli@systemli.org.

docs.title: Find something to work on
docs.text:
• Browse the issue tracker, especially good first issues.
  • Report a bug or suggest a feature.
  • For bigger changes, open an issue first to discuss the approach.
  • Security issues: please report them privately, see SECURITY.md.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Fork the repository and create a branch.
  2. Set up the development environment.
  3. Make your change. Follow the architecture conventions.
  4. Add or update tests, see Testing.
  5. Update the documentation for every audience that is affected – users, admins and operators, see Documentation.
  6. If operators have to do something when updating (new or removed environment variables, migrations with manual steps, changed Dovecot configuration), describe it in UPGRADE.md.
  7. Run the code quality checks (below) and open a pull request.

CI runs PHPUnit, Behat, Vitest, PHP CS Fixer, Rector, Psalm, migration checks and CodeQL on every pull request.

docs.title: Coding style
docs.text:
Code style is enforced by PHP CS Fixer, Rector, and Psalm.

makecomposer 
make lint    # check code style and Rector rules
make fix     # apply PHP CS Fixer and Rector fixes
make psalm   # static analysis

composer cs-check       # check code style
composer cs-fix         # fix code style
composer rector-check   # Rector dry-run
composer rector-fix     # apply Rector changes
composer psalm          # static analysis

For TypeScript:

yarn typecheck

Tip

Run all checks before pushing to catch issues early. CI will reject code that fails these checks.

docs.title: Commits
docs.text:
• Use Gitmojis in commit messages, e.g. ✨ Add alias notes or 🐛 Fix voucher count
  • Write commit messages in English

docs.title: Database changes
docs.text:
Change entities in src/Entity/ and generate a migration:

bin/console doctrine:migrations:diff

Review the generated SQL. Migrations must work on MariaDB and MySQL.

docs.title: Translations
docs.text: User-facing text always uses translation keys. Add new keys to the English and German files, see Translations.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: This documentation is built with MkDocs and Material for MkDocs. The sources are in docs/, the navigation is defined in mkdocs.yml. Every push to main publishes it to systemli.github.io/userli.

docs.title: Preview locally
docs.text:
With mise:

mise run docs

Without mise, with uv:

uvx --with-requirements docs/requirements.txt mkdocs serve --livereload --dev-addr 127.0.0.1:8100

Open http://127.0.0.1:8100. The page reloads automatically when you change a file. Port 8100 is used because the development environment already uses 8000 and 8001.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
The documentation is organized by audience:

Section Audience Writing style user/ Users of an email service No technical knowledge required. Explain what and why, use UI labels exactly as shown in English, avoid jargon. admin/ Admins and domain admins Familiar with the web interface, not necessarily with servers. Explain effects and consequences of actions. operations/ Server operators Linux, webserver, database and mail server knowledge. Give complete, copy-pasteable configuration. development/ Contributors Know PHP/Symfony. Point to code and conventions.

When documenting a feature, check whether every audience needs something: how users use it, how admins configure it, how operators enable it.

docs.title: Guidelines
docs.text:
• Write in English, short sentences, active voice.
  • Use admonitions (!!! note, !!! warning, !!! danger) for important information, especially for data loss.
  • Use relative links to other pages (../admin/settings.md#mta-sts). MkDocs checks them on build.
  • When moving a page, add a redirect in the redirects plugin section of mkdocs.yml, so that external links keep working.

  • Show screenshots with {class="screenshot"}:

    ![Users](../assets/images/admin-users.png){class="screenshot"}

  • Screenshots are taken with the example data from make fixtures and stored in docs/assets/images/.

docs.title: Release
docs.text: Release tarballs are the preferred way to distribute Userli. This page explains how to create a release.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Update CHANGELOG.md with a section for the new version. The date must match today's date in YYYY.MM.DD format:

    ## 6.3.0 (2026.03.01)

### Features and Improvements
- ...

  2. Commit and merge the changelog update before running the release script.

  3. You need a GitHub API token with the following scopes:

    public_repo, repo:status, repo_deployment

  4. You need a GPG key for signing the tag and tarballs.

docs.title: Create the release
docs.text:
Run the release script:

GITHUB_API_TOKEN=<token> GPG_SIGN_KEY="<key_id>" ./bin/github-release.sh <version>

The script will:

  • Validate that CHANGELOG.md contains the version with today's date
  • Create a GPG-signed git tag
  • Build two release tarballs via make release:
    • userli-<version>.tar.gz -- the main application
    • userli-dovecot-adapter-<version>.tar.gz -- the Dovecot Lua adapter
  • Generate SHA-256 and SHA-512 checksums
  • Create GPG-detached signatures (.asc) for both tarballs
  • Push the tag to origin
  • Create a GitHub Release with notes extracted from CHANGELOG.md
  • Upload all artifacts as release assets

docs.title: Docker image
docs.text: The Docker image (systemli/userli:latest) is published automatically to Docker Hub on every push to the main branch via GitHub Actions. This is separate from the tarball release process.

docs.title: PHPUnit
docs.text:
Unit tests mirror the src/ directory structure under tests/. Tests use SQLite (configured in .env.test), so no running database container is needed.

directmake 
bin/phpunit

make phpunit

docs.title: Vitest
docs.text:
Vitest with jsdom is used to unit-test Stimulus controllers and JavaScript/TypeScript utilities. Test files live in tests/js/ and mirror the assets/ structure.

directmake 
yarn test              # Single run
yarn test:watch        # Watch mode during development
yarn test:coverage     # Run with coverage report

make vitest

docs.title: Behat
docs.text:
Behat feature files are in features/. They test user-facing functionality through a browser simulation.

directmake 
bin/behat --format progress

make behat

docs.title: Dovecot integration
docs.text: Dovecot authenticates users and looks up mailbox info via Userli's HTTP API (/api/dovecot/). A Lua adapter (contrib/userli-dovecot-adapter.lua) sends requests with a Bearer token to Userli's DovecotController.

docs.title: Behat tests
docs.text:
The Dovecot API is tested automatically as part of the Behat suite in features/api_dovecot.feature. These tests run in CI without a real Dovecot instance -- they simulate the HTTP requests that Dovecot would make.

The scenarios cover:

  • Status -- API health check with valid and invalid tokens
  • Passdb -- password verification for valid users, wrong passwords, nonexistent users, and blocked (spam) users
  • Userdb -- mailbox lookup for existing users, nonexistent users, and spam users

To run only the Dovecot-related tests:

bin/behat --tags=@dovecot --format progress

docs.title: Mailcrypt integration test
docs.text:
A dedicated GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/mailcrypt.yml) tests the Dovecot mailcrypt integration end-to-end. It uses a separate compose file (docker-compose.mailcrypt-test.yml) that starts a real Dovecot instance with a Python mock of the Userli API (tests/dovecot-api-mock.py).

The test (tests/mailcrypt_integration.sh) uploads emails via IMAP to two users:

  • A user with mailcrypt enabled -- verifies that the email content is not readable on disk (encrypted)
  • A user without mailcrypt -- verifies that the email content is readable on disk (plaintext)

This ensures that the Lua adapter, Dovecot's mail_crypt plugin, and the API contract work correctly together.

To run the mailcrypt tests locally:

podmandocker 
COMPOSE_FILE=docker-compose.mailcrypt-test.yml podman compose up -d
bash tests/mailcrypt_integration.sh
COMPOSE_FILE=docker-compose.mailcrypt-test.yml podman compose down -v

COMPOSE_FILE=docker-compose.mailcrypt-test.yml docker compose up -d
bash tests/mailcrypt_integration.sh
COMPOSE_FILE=docker-compose.mailcrypt-test.yml docker compose down -v

docs.title: Manual testing with containers
docs.text:
The development containers are pre-configured to connect Dovecot to Userli's API. After loading the fixtures (see Getting started), you can test authentication from inside the Dovecot container:

podmandocker 
podman compose exec dovecot doveadm auth test user@example.org password

docker compose exec dovecot doveadm auth test user@example.org password

You can also test the full flow by connecting an IMAP client to localhost:1143 or by using Roundcube at http://localhost:8001.

See the Dovecot documentation for more context.

docs.title: Translations
docs.text: Userli is available in English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, Norwegian Bokmål and Swiss German.

docs.title: Translate on Weblate
docs.text:
All languages except English and German are translated on Weblate. You don't need to know Git or PHP – create a Weblate account and start translating. The maintainers merge the translations into the repository.

To add a new language, start it on Weblate and open an issue so that it can be added to the language switcher.

docs.title: English and German
docs.text:
English and German are maintained directly in the repository:

default_translations/
├── en/
│   ├── messages.en.yml     UI and email texts
│   └── validators.en.yml   Validation messages
└── de/
    ├── messages.de.yml
    └── validators.de.yml

When you add or change a user-facing text:

  1. Add the key to messages.en.yml and messages.de.yml.

  2. Use the key in templates with the |trans filter:

    {{ 'welcome.invitations.headline'|trans }}
{{ 'welcome.invitations.text'|trans({'%limit%': limit, '%waitingPeriodDays%': days}) }}

  3. In PHP, use the TranslatorInterface or pass translation keys to flash messages and constraints.

Never hard-code user-facing text in templates or code. Weblate picks up new English keys for the other languages automatically.

docs.title: Overriding texts in an installation
docs.text: Operators can override texts without changing the code, see Customization.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text: This part is for people who install and run Userli on a server and connect it to the mail server. You should be familiar with Linux administration, a webserver with PHP, MariaDB/MySQL and the basics of Postfix and Dovecot.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Userli is the account database and self-service portal of a mail system. It never touches mail directly: the mail server asks Userli via HTTP APIs.

flowchart TB
    subgraph web[Userli host]
        WS[Webserver<br/>Caddy / Nginx / Apache] --> FPM[PHP-FPM<br/>Userli]
        WK[Worker<br/>messenger:consume async]
        SC[Scheduler<br/>messenger:consume scheduler_maintenance]
        FPM --- DB[(MariaDB / MySQL)]
        WK --- DB
        SC --- DB
        FPM -.- RD[(Redis<br/>optional)]
    end
    subgraph mail[Mail host]
        PF[Postfix] --> PA[userli-postfix-adapter]
        DV[Dovecot] --> LUA[Lua adapter]
    end
    PA -->|/api/postfix| WS
    LUA -->|/api/dovecot| WS
    RC[Roundcube] -->|/api/roundcube| WS
    KC[Keycloak] -->|/api/keycloak| WS
    WK -->|SMTP| PF
    WK -->|webhooks| EXT[Other services]
Component Purpose Web application PHP application behind a webserver. Serves the user and admin interface, the APIs, the Web Key Directory and MTA-STS policies. Database MariaDB or MySQL. Stores users, aliases, domains, settings and the message queue. Worker Sends emails and webhooks asynchronously. Scheduler Triggers recurring maintenance tasks. Redis Optional shared cache – recommended when running several instances or containers. Dovecot Authenticates IMAP/POP3 users and gets mailbox encryption keys from Userli via a Lua adapter. Postfix Looks up domains, mailboxes, aliases, senders and SMTP quotas and authenticates SMTP users via the Postfix adapter.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
1. Check the requirements.
  2. Install Userli from a release tarball or with Ansible.
  3. Configure it, set up the webserver and the background services.
  4. Run the initial setup.
  5. Connect Dovecot and Postfix.
  6. Plan updates, backups and monitoring, and review the security notes.

The day-to-day management of users and domains in the web interface is described in the Admin Guide.

docs.title: Deploy with Ansible
docs.text:
We maintain the Ansible role systemli.userli and use it to run Userli at systemli.org. It automates the steps from Install from release and Updating.

The role targets Debian with a local MariaDB/MySQL server. Each role release pins a Userli version, so updating the role updates Userli.

docs.title: What the role does
docs.text:
• Downloads the release tarball, checks its SHA-512 checksum and unpacks it into /var/www/userli-x.y.z
  • Links /var/www/userli to the current release
  • Writes .env.local from userli_env_vars
  • Creates the database and the database user, and runs the migrations on the first run
  • Installs and starts the userli-worker and userli-scheduler systemd services
  • Deploys updates when you ask for it (see Updating)
  • Optionally installs a systemd timer that writes Prometheus metrics for the node exporter textfile collector (see Monitoring); it needs sponge from the moreutils package

The role does not install PHP, the webserver or the database server, and it does not write a webserver configuration. Set them up yourself (see Requirements and Webserver) or with other roles.

docs.title: Install the role
docs.text:
The role is published on Ansible Galaxy. Add it and the collections it uses to your requirements.yml:

requirements.yml
roles:
  - name: systemli.userli

collections:
  - community.general
  - ansible.mysql

ansible-galaxy install -r requirements.yml

docs.title: Example playbook
docs.text:
userli.yml
- name: Deploy Userli
  hosts: userli
  become: true
  roles:
    - systemli.userli
  vars:
    userli_mysql_password: "{{ vault_userli_mysql_password }}"
    userli_env_vars:
      - name: APP_ENV
        value: "prod"
      - name: APP_DEBUG
        value: "false"
      - name: APP_SECRET
        value: "{{ vault_userli_app_secret }}"
      - name: DATABASE_URL
        value: "{{ userli_db_url }}"
      - name: MAILER_DSN
        value: "smtp://localhost:25"
      - name: DEFAULT_URI
        value: "https://users.example.org"

Warning

userli_env_vars replaces the default list. Always set APP_SECRET and DATABASE_URL, and keep secrets in Ansible Vault. See Configuration for all variables.

The first run with -e userli_update=true installs Userli and warms up the cache:

ansible-playbook userli.yml -e userli_update=true

Then run the initial setup.

docs.title: Important variables
docs.text:
Variable Default Description userli_version latest release Userli version to install userli_mysql_password – Password of the database user (required) userli_mysql_user / userli_mysql_db userli Database user and name userli_env_vars minimal set Content of .env.local userli_home /var/www Directory for the releases userli_user / userli_group www-data System user that owns the application userli_webserver apache2 Webserver service stopped during updates userli_update false Deploy a new version (cache, migrations, restarts) userli_primary true Manage the database on this host userli_prometheus_textfile_collector_enabled false Install the metrics timer

See defaults/main.yml for all variables.

To customize texts or templates, put the files into a userli/ directory next to your playbook (for example userli/translations/en/messages.en.yml). The role copies them into the release directory.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
Read the release notes first, back up the database and update the role (or set userli_version). Then deploy with:

ansible-playbook userli.yml -e userli_update=true

With userli_update=true the role stops the webserver and the background services, clears and warms up the cache, runs the migrations and starts everything again.

Danger

Without userli_update=true, a new userli_version is still unpacked and /var/www/userli is switched to it, but the cache and the migrations are not updated. Always pass -e userli_update=true when the version changes.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
All API endpoints require an API token with the matching scope:

Authorization: Bearer <PLAIN_TOKEN>

Responses are JSON. A missing or invalid token results in 401, a token without the required scope in 403.

docs.title: Dovecot
docs.text:
Scope dovecot. Used by the Dovecot Lua adapter.

Method Path Description GET /api/dovecot/status Health check. Returns {"message": "success"}. GET /api/dovecot/{email} userdb lookup. POST /api/dovecot/{email} passdb lookup: verify the password.

userdb lookup response:

{
  "message": "success",
  "body": {
    "user": "user@example.org",
    "mailCrypt": 2,
    "mailCryptPublicKey": "<base64>",
    "quota": "1024M"
  }
}

mailCrypt is 2 if MailCrypt is enabled for the user, otherwise 0. quota is empty if no quota is set. Unknown and deleted users return 404.

passdb lookup request and response:

{ "password": "<password>" }

{
  "message": "success",
  "body": {
    "mailCrypt": 2,
    "mailCryptPrivateKey": "<base64>",
    "mailCryptPublicKey": "<base64>"
  }
}
Status Meaning 200 Authenticated 401 Wrong password 403 Role Spam or password change required 404 Unknown or deleted user 500 MailCrypt key could not be decrypted

docs.title: Postfix
docs.text:
Scope postfix. Used by the Postfix adapter.

Method Path Response GET /api/postfix/domain/{domain} true if the domain is managed by Userli GET /api/postfix/mailbox/{email} true if an active user with this address exists GET /api/postfix/alias/{email} List of destinations of the alias, e.g. ["user@example.org"] GET /api/postfix/senders/{email} List of users allowed to send with this address GET /api/postfix/smtp_quota/{email} {"per_hour": 100, "per_day": 1000}, 0 = unlimited; 404 for unknown users POST /api/postfix/auth SMTP authentication, body {"email": "...", "password": "..."}

auth status codes: 200 success, 401 authentication failed, 403 role Spam or password change required.

docs.title: Roundcube
docs.text:
Scope roundcube. Used by the Roundcube plugin.

Method Path Description POST /api/roundcube/aliases Body {"email": "...", "password": "..."}. Returns the list of the user's alias addresses. 401 on wrong credentials. App passwords are rejected.

docs.title: Keycloak
docs.text:
Scope keycloak. Used by the Keycloak user provider.

Method Path Description GET /api/keycloak/{domain}?search=&max=10&first=0 Search users. Returns [{"id": "<local part>", "email": "..."}]. GET /api/keycloak/{domain}/count Number of users in the domain. GET /api/keycloak/{domain}/user/{email} Get a single user. POST /api/keycloak/{domain}/validate/{email} Validate a credential, body {"credentialType": "password"\|"otp", "password": "..."}. App passwords are rejected. GET /api/keycloak/{domain}/configured/{credentialType}/{email} Whether the user has the credential type (e.g. otp) configured.

For otp, password is the 6-digit TOTP code or a backup code – a matching backup code is consumed. See Keycloak for status codes.

docs.title: Retention
docs.text:
Scope retention. See Retention.

Method Path Description PUT /api/retention/{email}/touch Update the last login time. Optional body {"timestamp": <unix time>}; 400 if in the future. GET /api/retention/users List users without login for two years.

docs.title: Public endpoints
docs.text:
No authentication required.

Method Path Description GET /.well-known/openpgpkey/{domain}/hu/{hash} Web Key Directory: binary OpenPGP key GET /.well-known/openpgpkey/{domain}/policy Web Key Directory policy (empty) GET /.well-known/mta-sts.txt MTA-STS policy for the domain in the Host header

docs.title: Background services
docs.text:
Besides the webserver, Userli needs two long-running processes:

Process Command Purpose Worker bin/console messenger:consume async Sends emails (welcome, recovery, notifications, reports) and webhooks, and runs the maintenance tasks. Scheduler bin/console messenger:consume scheduler_maintenance Triggers the recurring maintenance tasks on schedule.

Warning

Without the worker, no emails and no webhooks are sent and maintenance tasks never run. Without the scheduler, maintenance tasks only run when started manually in Admin → Maintenance.

Both processes should be restarted regularly to free memory and to pick up new code after updates. The --time-limit option makes them exit after the given number of seconds; the process supervisor starts them again.

docs.title: systemd
docs.text:
Create one unit per process. Adjust user, path and PHP binary.

/etc/systemd/system/userli-worker.service
[Unit]
Description=Userli worker
After=network.target mariadb.service

[Service]
User=userli
Group=userli
WorkingDirectory=/var/www/userli
ExecStart=/usr/bin/php bin/console messenger:consume async --time-limit=3600 --memory-limit=128M
Restart=always
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
/etc/systemd/system/userli-scheduler.service
[Unit]
Description=Userli scheduler
After=network.target mariadb.service

[Service]
User=userli
Group=userli
WorkingDirectory=/var/www/userli
ExecStart=/usr/bin/php bin/console messenger:consume scheduler_maintenance --time-limit=3600 --memory-limit=128M
Restart=always
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

Enable and start them:

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now userli-worker userli-scheduler

docs.title: Queue
docs.text:
Queued messages are stored in the database by default. To use Redis or AMQP, set MESSENGER_TRANSPORT_DSN, see Configuration.

Failed messages are retried three times (after 10 seconds, 1 minute and 6 minutes). To inspect the queue:

bin/console messenger:stats

docs.title: Scheduler state
docs.text: The scheduler remembers when tasks ran last. If it was not running, it catches up missed tasks on start. The state is stored in the cache – with several hosts or containers, use Redis so that all share the same state. Run only one scheduler process.

docs.title: What to back up
docs.text:
Data Where Why Database MariaDB/MySQL database userli All accounts, aliases, domains, settings, password hashes and the encrypted MailCrypt keys. Configuration .env.local or your environment variables Especially APP_SECRET and DATABASE_URL. Customizations translations/ in the installation directory Overridden texts, if any.

The application code can be downloaded again and doesn't need a backup. The cache (var/cache) and Redis contain no data that can't be rebuilt.

Database and mailboxes belong together

With MailCrypt, the keys to decrypt the mailboxes are only stored in the Userli database. Without a database backup, encrypted mailboxes can't be read anymore. Back up the database at least as often as the mailboxes and keep both for the same period.

Backups contain sensitive data

Database backups contain password hashes and encrypted private keys. Encrypt them and restrict access.

docs.title: Database backup
docs.text:
mysqldump --single-transaction --routines --triggers userli | gzip > userli-$(date +%F).sql.gz

Run it regularly, for example as a systemd timer or cron job, and copy the backups to another host.

docs.title: Restore
docs.text:
1. Install the same Userli version that was running when the backup was made (see Install from release).
  2. Restore the configuration (.env.local).

  3. Restore the database:

    gunzip -c userli-2025-01-01.sql.gz | mysql userli

  4. Clear the cache and start the services:

    bin/console cache:clear

  5. If you want to update to a newer version, do it afterwards as described in Updating.

docs.title: Console commands
docs.text:
Userli ships with console commands for tasks that are not available in the web interface or that are useful for scripts. Run them from the installation directory as the user that owns the files:

bin/console <command> --help

In containers, prefix them with docker compose exec userli.

Commands that change users support --dry-run to show what would happen.

docs.title: Users
docs.text: Command Description app:admin:password [password] Set the password of postmaster@<default domain>. Creates the account (and domain) if missing. app:users:delete --user <email> Delete a user (soft delete). app:users:restore --user <email> Restore a deleted user. app:users:reset --user <email> Reset a user: new password, new MailCrypt keys, new recovery token, 2FA off. Existing encrypted emails become unreadable. app:users:quota --user <email> Show the mailbox quota of a user. app:users:mailcrypt --user <email> [password] Show the MailCrypt values of a user. app:users:registration:mail --user <email> [--locale de] Send the welcome email again.

docs.title: Aliases and invite codes
docs.text: Command Description app:alias:delete --alias <email> [--user <email>] Delete an alias. app:voucher:create --user <email> [--count 3] [--domain <domain>] [--print] [--print-links] Create invite codes for a user and optionally print the codes or registration links. app:voucher:count --user <email> Show used and unused invite codes of a user.

docs.title: Domains
docs.text: Command Description app:domain:delete --domain <domain> Delete a domain and all its users, aliases and invite codes. Try --dry-run first.

docs.title: OpenPGP keys
docs.text: Command Description app:openpgp:import-key <email> <file> Import and publish a key for an address. app:openpgp:show-key <email> Show the published key of an address. app:openpgp:delete-key <email> Delete the published key of an address.

docs.title: API tokens
docs.text: Command Description app:api-token:create --name <name> --scopes <scope> [--scopes <scope>] Create a token. Scopes: dovecot, postfix, roundcube, keycloak, retention. Prints the plain token once. app:api-token:delete --token <plain token> Delete a token.

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text: Command Description app:metrics Print metrics in Prometheus format, see Monitoring.

docs.title: Useful Symfony commands
docs.text: Command Description doctrine:migrations:migrate Apply database migrations. doctrine:migrations:status Show the migration status. cache:clear Clear the cache, for example after changing .env.local or translations. messenger:consume async Run the worker. messenger:consume scheduler_maintenance Run the scheduler. messenger:stats Show the number of queued messages. messenger:failed:show Show failed messages. debug:scheduler Show the scheduled maintenance tasks.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Userli is configured in two places:

  • Environment variables for everything the server needs to start – database, mail transport, secrets. Described on this page.
  • Settings in the admin interface for everything that can change at runtime – names, URLs, sender addresses, MailCrypt, MTA-STS. See Admin Guide → Settings.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: The file .env in the installation directory contains the defaults with comments. Don't edit it – it is replaced on updates. Instead, create .env.local next to it, or set real environment variables (for example in containers or systemd units). Real environment variables take precedence over both files.

docs.title: Required
docs.text: Variable Description Example APP_ENV Environment. Always prod on servers. prod APP_SECRET Random secret used for CSRF tokens and to sign queued messages. Keep it secret and stable. output of openssl rand -hex 32 DATABASE_URL Database connection. Add serverVersion to match your database. mysql://userli:pass@127.0.0.1:3306/userli?serverVersion=mariadb-10.11.0 MAILER_DSN How Userli sends emails, see Symfony Mailer. smtp://localhost:25

docs.title: Recommended
docs.text:
Variable Description Example DEFAULT_URI Public base URL. Needed to generate correct links in emails sent by the worker. https://users.example.org MESSENGER_TRANSPORT_DSN Queue for asynchronous messages. The default in .env uses the database; Redis or AMQP are possible, see Symfony Messenger. redis://localhost:6379/messages REDIS_URL Enables Redis as cache. redis://localhost:6379 SYMFONY_TRUSTED_PROXIES IP addresses or ranges of reverse proxies in front of Userli, see Security. 127.0.0.1,REMOTE_ADDR

Changing APP_SECRET

Messages in the queue are signed with APP_SECRET. If you change it, let the worker process all queued messages first, otherwise they are rejected.

docs.title: Removed variables
docs.text:
These variables were used by older versions and are ignored now. Remove them from your configuration:

Variable Replaced by REGISTRATION_OPEN Invitations per domain (6.6.0) MAIL_CRYPT Setting MailCrypt (6.4.0) WEBMAIL_URL Setting Webmail URL (6.2.0) DOVECOT_API_*, KEYCLOAK_API_*, RETENTION_API_* API tokens

docs.title: Cache
docs.text:
By default, Userli uses the filesystem for caching. This works well for small installations on a single host.

For larger installations, Redis is recommended as a shared cache backend. Set REDIS_URL:

REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379

When REDIS_URL is set, Userli automatically switches from filesystem to Redis for all caching (application cache, Doctrine result cache, scheduler state, etc.).

Note

The PHP Redis extension (phpredis) must be installed for the Redis adapter to work. It is included in the official container image.

Warning

If you run multiple containers (web, worker, scheduler) without Redis, each container maintains its own isolated filesystem cache. This means cache invalidation in one container does not affect the others.

After changing environment variables, clear the cache:

bin/console cache:clear

docs.title: Names, URLs and addresses
docs.text: Application name, project name and URLs, sender addresses and the webmail link are settings in the admin interface.

docs.title: Texts
docs.text:
All texts of the web interface and of the emails come from translation files. The defaults are in default_translations/<lang>/messages.<lang>.yml and validators.<lang>.yml. They are replaced on every update – don't edit them.

To change a text, override its key in translations/<lang>/messages.<lang>.yml in the installation directory. You only need to include the keys you want to change:

translations/en/messages.en.yml
welcome:
  custom-bottom: >
    <h3>Need help?</h3>
    <p>Visit our <a href="https://www.example.org/help">help pages</a>.</p>

Clear the cache afterwards:

bin/console cache:clear

Look up the key of a text in default_translations/en/messages.en.yml. Override every language you offer – missing keys fall back to the default text of that language, then to English.

Useful keys:

Key Where welcome.custom-bottom Additional block at the bottom of the welcome page after registration. Empty by default. HTML is allowed and sanitized. mail.welcome-body Welcome email. Placeholders %quota_text% and %invitation_text% are filled from mail.welcome-quota, mail.welcome-quota-unlimited and mail.welcome-invitations (the latter is omitted if invitations are disabled for the user's domain).

Note

Keep your translations/ directory when updating, see Updating.

docs.title: Languages
docs.text: Userli ships with English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, Bokmål and Swiss German. Translations are maintained on Weblate – improvements there benefit everybody. See Translations.

docs.title: Run with containers
docs.text:
A container image is published on Docker Hub as systemli/userli.

Not recommended for production

We use the container image and the Compose setup for local development only. They are not intended for production, are not maintained to production standards and have not been hardened for it. For production, install Userli from a release tarball.

Only latest

The image is built from the main branch on every push and only tagged latest (for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64). There are no version tags yet. If you use it anyway, pin the image by digest and test updates before deploying them.

docs.title: The image
docs.text:
• Based on php:8.4-fpm-alpine, it runs PHP-FPM on port 9000 (FastCGI). You need a webserver in front of it, for example Caddy.
  • The application lives in /var/www/html, the document root is /var/www/html/public.
  • It includes the PHP extensions gd, intl, opcache, pdo_mysql, redis, sodium and zip, plus GnuPG.
  • It does not run database migrations on start. Run them after each update.
  • Configuration is done with environment variables.

The same image is used for three containers: the web application, the worker and the scheduler.

docs.title: Example with Compose
docs.text:
This example runs Userli with Caddy, MariaDB and Redis. Adjust passwords, domains and TLS to your needs.

compose.yml
x-userli: &userli
  image: docker.io/systemli/userli:latest
  restart: unless-stopped
  environment:
    APP_ENV: prod
    APP_SECRET: change-me
    DATABASE_URL: mysql://userli:change-me@mariadb:3306/userli?serverVersion=mariadb-10.11.0
    MAILER_DSN: smtp://mail.example.org:25
    DEFAULT_URI: https://users.example.org
    REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379
  depends_on:
    - mariadb
    - redis

services:
  userli:
    <<: *userli
    volumes:
      - public:/var/www/html/public

  userli-worker:
    <<: *userli
    command: php bin/console messenger:consume async --time-limit=3600

  userli-scheduler:
    <<: *userli
    command: php bin/console messenger:consume scheduler_maintenance --time-limit=3600

  caddy:
    image: docker.io/caddy:2-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - ./Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro
      - public:/var/www/html/public:ro
      - caddy_data:/data

  mariadb:
    image: docker.io/mariadb:10.11
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      MARIADB_DATABASE: userli
      MARIADB_USER: userli
      MARIADB_PASSWORD: change-me
      MARIADB_RANDOM_ROOT_PASSWORD: "yes"
    volumes:
      - mariadb:/var/lib/mysql

  redis:
    image: docker.io/redis:7-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  public:
  mariadb:
  caddy_data:
Caddyfile
users.example.org {
    root * /var/www/html/public
    php_fastcgi userli:9000
    file_server
}

The public volume shares the static files (CSS, JavaScript, images) of the image with Caddy.

Static files after updates

A named volume is only filled from the image when it is created. After updating the image, remove the public volume (or copy the files) so that Caddy serves the new assets.

Start the containers and create the database schema:

docker compose up -d
docker compose exec userli bin/console doctrine:migrations:migrate --no-interaction

Continue with the initial setup.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d
docker compose exec userli bin/console doctrine:migrations:migrate --no-interaction

Read Updating before each update.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text: In production, Userli logs errors to syslog with the ident userli. A container usually has no syslog daemon, so only deprecation messages reach stderr. Use the worker output and the webserver logs, or mount a syslog socket into the container. See Monitoring and logs.

docs.title: Initial setup
docs.text: After installing Userli, creating the database schema and configuring the webserver and the background services, finish the setup in the browser.

docs.title: Setup wizard
docs.text:
Open Userli in your browser. As long as no domain exists, you are redirected to the setup wizard at /init, which guides you through three steps:

  1. Create the first mail domain. It becomes the default domain.

  2. Set the password of the first admin account postmaster@<domain>.

  3. Configure the basic settings. The form is prefilled based on the domain, for example https://users.<domain> as App URL and noreply@<domain> as sender address. Check at least:

    • App name and App URL
    • Project name and Project URL
    • Sender address and Notification address
    • Webmail URL, if you offer webmail
    • Postmaster address and Abuse address

Afterwards, sign in with the admin account. All settings can be changed later in Admin → Settings.

You can also set the admin password on the command line:

bin/console app:admin:password

docs.title: Import reserved names
docs.text: Prevent users from registering addresses like admin or abuse: import the curated list contrib/reserved_names.txt in Admin → Reserved Names → Import. See Reserved names.

docs.title: Enable invitations
docs.text: New users can only register with invite codes. Enable invitations for your domain in Admin → Domains → Edit and create the first invite codes. See Invite codes.

docs.title: Connect the mail server
docs.text:
• Dovecot – authentication and mailbox encryption
  • Postfix – domains, mailboxes, aliases, SMTP authentication

docs.title: Removing mailboxes of deleted users
docs.text: Userli has no access to the mailboxes on the mail server (usually owned by the system user vmail) and therefore does not delete them. To remove the mailbox of a deleted account, react to the user.deleted webhook on the mail server. The mailbox janitor does this for you and also purges mailboxes of reset accounts.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• Background services (worker and scheduler) are running
  • Settings reviewed
  • Reserved names imported
  • Dovecot and Postfix connected and tested
  • Backups configured
  • Monitoring configured

docs.title: Install from release
docs.text:
Release tarballs are the recommended way to install Userli on a server. They contain the application, all PHP dependencies and the built frontend assets.

The steps below assume Debian/Ubuntu, a system user userli and the installation directory /var/www/userli. Adjust them to your system.

Tip

To automate these steps, use our Ansible role.

docs.title: 1. Download
docs.text:
Get the latest release. Each release provides userli-x.y.z.tar.gz, SHA-256/SHA-512 checksums and a GPG signature (.asc).

cd /tmp
wget https://github.com/systemli/userli/releases/download/x.y.z/userli-x.y.z.tar.gz
wget https://github.com/systemli/userli/releases/download/x.y.z/userli-x.y.z.tar.gz.sha256
wget https://github.com/systemli/userli/releases/download/x.y.z/userli-x.y.z.tar.gz.sha256.asc

# Verify the signature of the hashsum file
gpg --verify userli-x.y.z.tar.gz.sha256.asc userli-x.y.z.tar.gz.sha256

# Verify the hash of the release tarball against the hashsum file
sha256sum -c userli-x.y.z.tar.gz.sha256

Tip

Check the exact file names on the release page. To verify the signature, import the release signing key first.

Unpack it:

sudo mkdir -p /var/www/userli
sudo tar -xzf userli-x.y.z.tar.gz -C /var/www/userli --strip-components=1
sudo chown -R userli:userli /var/www/userli

docs.title: 2. Create the database
docs.text:
Create a database and a database user:

sudo mysql -e 'CREATE DATABASE userli CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci'
sudo mysql -e "CREATE USER 'userli'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY '<password>'"
sudo mysql -e "GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON userli.* TO 'userli'@'localhost'"

docs.title: 3. Configure
docs.text:
Create /var/www/userli/.env.local with at least these values. See Configuration for all options.

APP_ENV=prod
APP_SECRET=<random string, e.g. from: openssl rand -hex 32>
DATABASE_URL="mysql://userli:<password>@127.0.0.1:3306/userli?serverVersion=mariadb-10.11.0"
MAILER_DSN=smtp://localhost:25
DEFAULT_URI=https://users.example.org

docs.title: 4. Create the schema
docs.text:
cd /var/www/userli
sudo -u userli bin/console doctrine:migrations:migrate --no-interaction
sudo -u userli bin/console cache:warmup

docs.title: 5. Next steps
docs.text:
1. Configure the webserver with the document root /var/www/userli/public.
  2. Start the background services.
  3. Run the initial setup.

docs.title: MailCrypt
docs.text:
Userli has built-in support for Dovecot's mailbox encryption, using the global keys mode. Each user has their own key pair. New emails are encrypted with the public key when they are stored. Only with the user's password – or recovery token – can the private key be unlocked to read them.

Keys are created and maintained by Userli and handed over to Dovecot by the Lua adapter on each login.

docs.title: What it protects – and what not
docs.text:
• Protected: emails at rest on the mail server's disk and in backups. An attacker who gets the files, or an admin who browses them, can't read them without the user's password.
  • Not protected: emails in transit, Dovecot's index and cache files (they can contain metadata such as senders and subjects), folder names, sizes and timestamps, and emails while the user is logged in. The server sees the plain password at login, so an attacker who controls the running server can read the mailbox.
  • Consequence: if a user loses both password and recovery token, the emails are lost. Admins can't recover them.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
MailCrypt is configured globally in the admin interface under Admin → Settings → Mailbox Encryption (setting mail_crypt, default 2):

Value Meaning 0 Disable MailCrypt globally 1 Allow MailCrypt; keys are created, but it needs to be enabled manually per user 2 Enforce MailCrypt for new users (recommended) 3 Enforce MailCrypt key generation for all users – see migrating legacy users

The admin interface shows for every user whether MailCrypt is enabled:

MailCrypt can be turned on/off for individual users with the mail_crypt column in the users database table. This is mainly meant as migration path for legacy users without MailCrypt keys. On new setups, keep MailCrypt enabled for all users.

docs.title: Effects on account management
docs.text: Action Effect on encrypted emails User changes password Private key is re-encrypted. Emails stay readable. User recovers account with recovery token Private key is unlocked with the token and re-encrypted. Emails stay readable. Admin sets a new password New key pair. Existing emails become unreadable. Admin restores a deleted user New key pair. Old emails are unreadable.

docs.title: Implementation details
docs.text:
Userli uses elliptic curve keys with curve secp521r1, created with the openssl command line tool. The private key is encrypted with an Argon2i hash of the user's password, stored in a libsodium secret box.

A second copy of the private key is encrypted with an Argon2i hash of the user's recovery token. It is used when a user restores their account after they lost their password.

docs.title: Migrating legacy users
docs.text:
Legacy users (without MailCrypt keys) continue to work without mailbox encryption. If they generate a recovery token in the account settings, a MailCrypt key pair is created for them. This doesn't enable MailCrypt for them automatically, because this would result in accounts with partially unencrypted (old) and partially encrypted (new) emails. Enabling it is left to the server operators.

To enable MailCrypt for a legacy user:

  1. Ensure that they have a recovery token. This automatically creates a MailCrypt key pair. Only the account holder can do this, as the password is required.
  2. Set mail_crypt=1 for the user in the users database table.

To enforce MailCrypt for all legacy users:

  1. Set the MailCrypt setting to 3. A key pair is created automatically when legacy users log in the next time. Again, the user password is required for this.
