  2. Set mail_crypt=1 for all users that have a key pair but MailCrypt not enabled yet, for example with a regular cron job.

Existing emails are not encrypted. They stay unencrypted, and only new emails are stored encrypted.

The following SQL statement enables MailCrypt for all legacy users that have a key pair. Use with caution!

UPDATE users SET mail_crypt=1 WHERE mail_crypt_secret_box IS NOT NULL AND mail_crypt = 0;

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
Get the MailCrypt values of a user (requires the user's password):

bin/console app:users:mailcrypt --user user@example.org

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
bin/console app:metrics prints metrics in the Prometheus text format:

Metric Description userli_users_total All users, including deleted userli_users_active_total Users that are not deleted userli_users_deleted_total Deleted users userli_users_weekly_active_total Users with login in the last 7 days userli_users_monthly_active_total Users with login in the last 30 days userli_users_recovery_token_total Users with a recovery token userli_users_mailcrypt_total Users with MailCrypt enabled userli_users_twofactor_total Users with 2FA enabled userli_users_app_password_total Users with at least one app password userli_app_passwords_total App passwords userli_vouchers_total{type="redeemed"\|"unredeemed"} Invite codes userli_domains_total Domains userli_aliases_total Aliases userli_openpgpkeys_total Published OpenPGP keys

There is no HTTP endpoint. Use the textfile collector of the node exporter, for example with a cron job (sponge is part of moreutils):

/etc/cron.d/userli-metrics
* * * * * userli cd /var/www/userli && bin/console app:metrics | sponge /var/lib/prometheus/node-exporter/userli.prom

docs.title: What to monitor
docs.text:
• Webserver and PHP-FPM – availability of the start page via HTTPS.
  • Worker and scheduler – the processes are running. Check that the queue doesn't grow: bin/console messenger:stats.
  • Failed messages – bin/console messenger:failed:show.
  • Failed webhook deliveries – in Admin → Webhooks → Deliveries.
  • Integrations – login failures in Dovecot and Postfix logs, metrics of the Postfix adapter.
  • Certificates – including mta-sts.<domain> and openpgpkey.<domain>.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
Log Where Application errors syslog, ident userli, JSON format. Only errors are written – with the 50 log entries before each error for context. 404 and 405 errors are ignored. Deprecations stderr of PHP-FPM, JSON format Worker and scheduler stdout/stderr of the processes, e.g. journalctl -u userli-worker Requests webserver access log 
journalctl -t userli

In containers without a syslog daemon, application errors are not visible. Mount /dev/log from the host into the container, or check the worker output.

The weekly report emails new registrations to the notification address and is useful to notice spam waves.

docs.title: MTA-STS
docs.text:
Userli supports MTA-STS (SMTP MTA Strict Transport Security), a mechanism that allows mail domains to declare that they support TLS for inbound SMTP connections. Sending servers will refuse to deliver email without a valid TLS connection, protecting against downgrade and man-in-the-middle attacks.

MTA-STS is configured globally in the admin interface under Admin → Settings → MTA-STS (see Admin Guide → Settings). The following settings are available:

  • MTA-STS Mode — testing (default), enforce, or none
  • MX Hosts — allowed MX hostnames, one per line (e.g. mail.example.org, wildcards like *.example.org allowed). No policy is served while this list is empty.
  • Max Age — policy cache duration in seconds (default: 604800 = 1 week, minimum 1 day, maximum 1 year)

Userli serves the MTA-STS policy at /.well-known/mta-sts.txt, returning the policy for the domain derived from the Host header.

The controller extracts the domain from the Host header by stripping the mta-sts. prefix (e.g. mta-sts.example.org → example.org) and validates it against configured domains. If the domain is unknown, a 404 response is returned.

docs.title: Example Policy Response
docs.text:
version: STSv1
mode: enforce
mx: mail.example.org
mx: backup.example.org
max_age: 604800

docs.title: DNS Configuration
docs.text: MTA-STS requires two DNS records per domain.

docs.title: MTA-STS Subdomain
docs.text:
Point mta-sts.{domain} to your Userli server:

mta-sts.example.org.  IN CNAME  users.example.org.

docs.title: MTA-STS TXT Record
docs.text:
Advertise MTA-STS support. The id value must be updated whenever the policy changes:

_mta-sts.example.org.  IN TXT  "v=STSv1; id=20250227T000000;"

docs.title: TLSRPT (Optional)
docs.text:
Enable TLS reporting (RFC 8460) to receive reports about TLS delivery failures:

_smtp._tls.example.org.  IN TXT  "v=TLSRPTv1; rua=mailto:tlsrpt@example.org;"

docs.title: TLS Certificate
docs.text:
The TLS certificate must be valid for mta-sts.{domain}. If you use Let's Encrypt, add the subdomain to your certificate:

certbot certonly -d users.example.org -d mta-sts.example.org

docs.title: Reverse Proxy Setup
docs.text: The mta-sts.{domain} subdomain must be proxied to the Userli application. Ensure the Host header is forwarded so that Userli can identify the domain. Replace upstream and localhost:8000 with the address of your Userli webserver.

docs.title: Nginx
docs.text:
server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    server_name mta-sts.example.org;

    ssl_certificate     /etc/letsencrypt/live/users.example.org/fullchain.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/users.example.org/privkey.pem;

    location /.well-known/mta-sts.txt {
        proxy_pass http://upstream;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
    }
}

docs.title: Apache 2
docs.text:
<VirtualHost *:443>
    ServerName mta-sts.example.org

    SSLEngine On
    SSLCertificateFile    /etc/letsencrypt/live/users.example.org/fullchain.pem
    SSLCertificateKeyFile /etc/letsencrypt/live/users.example.org/privkey.pem

    ProxyPreserveHost On
    ProxyPass "/.well-known/mta-sts.txt" "http://localhost:8000/.well-known/mta-sts.txt"
    ProxyPassReverse "/.well-known/mta-sts.txt" "http://localhost:8000/.well-known/mta-sts.txt"
</VirtualHost>

docs.title: Caddy
docs.text:
mta-sts.example.org {
    handle /.well-known/mta-sts.txt {
        reverse_proxy localhost:8000
    }
    respond 404
}

docs.title: Userli host
docs.text:
• A webserver with PHP-FPM, for example Caddy, Nginx or Apache
  • PHP 8.4 with the extensions
    • sodium (mailbox encryption)
    • intl
    • pdo_mysql
    • gd, zip, opcache (recommended)
    • redis (optional, for the Redis cache)
  • MariaDB or MySQL
  • OpenSSL command line tool (openssl) – used to create MailCrypt keys
  • GnuPG 2.1.14 or newer – used to validate uploaded OpenPGP keys
  • A process supervisor such as systemd for the background services
  • An SMTP server to send emails (welcome mails, notifications, reports)
  • HTTPS with a valid certificate

Database support

Only MariaDB and MySQL are supported. The database migrations use MySQL-specific SQL, so PostgreSQL and SQLite can't be upgraded between releases.

Node.js and Composer are not needed: the release tarball contains all PHP dependencies and the built frontend assets.

docs.title: Mail host
docs.text:
• Dovecot 2.4 with Lua support (dovecot-auth-lua) and lua-json – for authentication and MailCrypt
  • Postfix with socketmap support and the userli-postfix-adapter (requires Redis)

Userli, Dovecot and Postfix can run on the same host or on different hosts. The mail host needs HTTPS access to Userli.

docs.title: Optional
docs.text:
• Roundcube with the Userli plugin
  • Keycloak with the Userli user provider for single sign-on
  • Prometheus node exporter for metrics

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Userli manages credentials and encryption keys. This page collects the security-relevant points for operators.

docs.title: Reporting vulnerabilities
docs.text: Please report security issues privately as described in SECURITY.md, not in public issues.

docs.title: HTTPS
docs.text: Always serve Userli, mta-sts.<domain> and openpgpkey.<domain> via HTTPS only and enable HSTS (see Webserver). The Dovecot and Postfix adapters send user passwords to Userli – use HTTPS for these connections, too, or keep them on a trusted local network.

docs.title: Reverse proxies
docs.text:
If Userli runs behind a reverse proxy or load balancer, tell it which proxies to trust. Otherwise, Userli sees the proxy's IP address instead of the client's and may generate http:// links:

SYMFONY_TRUSTED_PROXIES=127.0.0.1,10.0.0.0/8

REMOTE_ADDR trusts the directly connected client – only use it if Userli can't be reached without passing the proxy. The trusted headers can be set with SYMFONY_TRUSTED_HEADERS. See Symfony: How to configure Symfony to work behind a load balancer or a reverse proxy.

docs.title: Brute-force protection
docs.text:
Userli doesn't limit the number of login attempts. Protect the login and API endpoints at the webserver or with a tool like fail2ban or CrowdSec:

  • POST /login – web login
  • POST /2fa_check – two-factor codes
  • POST /recovery – recovery tokens

Failed SMTP and IMAP logins are visible in the Postfix and Dovecot logs.

docs.title: API tokens
docs.text:
• Create one API token per service with only the scopes it needs.
  • Tokens are stored hashed. Store the plain tokens like passwords.
  • Restrict access to /api/ to the IP addresses of your mail servers in the webserver, if possible.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
• APP_SECRET signs CSRF tokens and queued messages. Keep it secret and back it up.
  • Restrict file permissions of .env.local to the Userli user.

docs.title: Passwords and accounts
docs.text:
• Passwords need at least 12 characters and are checked against Have I Been Pwned on registration and change, and regularly on login (see Notifications). Only a hash prefix leaves the server. Userli needs outgoing HTTPS access to api.pwnedpasswords.com for this.
  • Password recovery has a 48-hour waiting period and notifies the user by email.
  • Use roles Spam and Suspicious to stop abuse quickly.

docs.title: Content Security Policy
docs.text: Userli sends a strict Content Security Policy and other security headers. If you add custom content (for example in translations), it must not rely on inline scripts or external resources.

docs.title: The setup wizard doesn't appear / redirect loop to /init
docs.text:
The wizard at /init is shown as long as no domain exists. If the database schema is missing, run the migrations first:

bin/console doctrine:migrations:migrate --no-interaction

docs.title: No emails are sent
docs.text:
• Check that the worker is running: systemctl status userli-worker.

  • Check the queue and failed messages:

    bin/console messenger:stats
bin/console messenger:failed:show

  • Check MAILER_DSN and the log of your SMTP server.

  • Check the Sender address in Admin → Settings. Your SMTP server must accept it.

docs.title: Links in emails point to localhost
docs.text: Set DEFAULT_URI to the public URL of Userli and restart the worker. Also check App URL in Admin → Settings.

docs.title: Userli generates http:// links behind a proxy
docs.text: Configure trusted proxies.

docs.title: Maintenance tasks don't run
docs.text: The scheduler must be running in addition to the worker. bin/console debug:scheduler shows the next run of each task.

docs.title: Dovecot login fails
docs.text:
• Test from the Dovecot host: doveadm auth test user@example.org.
  • Enable auth_debug = yes in Dovecot and check its log.
  • Check that USERLI_HOST and USERLI_API_ACCESS_TOKEN are set and imported with import_environment.

  • Test the API directly:

    curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" https://users.example.org/api/dovecot/status

    {"message":"success"} means the token works. 401 means the token is invalid, 403 that it lacks the dovecot scope.

  • The account may be deleted, have the role Spam or require a password change. Check it in Admin → Users.

docs.title: New users can't receive mail with MailCrypt
docs.text: Make sure crypt_write_algorithm is empty in the global Dovecot configuration, see Dovecot → MailCrypt.

docs.title: Changes don't reach Postfix immediately
docs.text: Lookups are cached for a few minutes by Userli and the Postfix adapter. Wait or restart the adapter.

docs.title: Users get "Registration closed"
docs.text: Invitations are disabled for the domain of the invite code. Enable them in Admin → Domains → Edit, see Invitations.

docs.title: Cache problems after an update or configuration change
docs.text:
bin/console cache:clear

With several containers but without Redis, each container has its own cache. Use Redis.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
The webserver/PHP-FPM user needs write access to var/ (cache and sessions). All other files can be read-only.

On systems with SELinux, also check the SELinux context of the installation directory.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
Userli follows semantic versioning. Read the release notes before every update:

  • CHANGELOG.md – all changes per release
  • UPGRADE.md – manual steps required for a release, for example removed environment variables or changed Dovecot configuration

Don't skip the notes of intermediate versions when updating over several releases.

docs.title: Update a tarball installation
docs.text:
1. Back up the database (see Backup and restore).
  2. Stop the background services and let the queue drain if UPGRADE.md says so.
  3. Download and verify the new release, see Install from release.
  4. Unpack it into a new directory and copy your .env.local (and translations/, if you customized texts) into it.

  5. Run the migrations and warm up the cache:

    bin/console doctrine:migrations:migrate --no-interaction
bin/console cache:clear

  6. Switch the webserver to the new directory (for example with a symlink /var/www/userli → /var/www/userli-x.y.z) and reload PHP-FPM.

  7. Start the background services again.
  8. Update the Dovecot adapter to the same version.

Using one directory per version makes rollbacks of the code easy. Rolling back database migrations is usually not possible – restore the backup instead.

docs.title: Update with Ansible
docs.text: See Deploy with Ansible.

docs.title: Update a container installation
docs.text: See Run with containers.

docs.title: Check the migration status
docs.text: bin/console doctrine:migrations:status

docs.title: Webserver
docs.text:
Userli is a Symfony application and runs behind any webserver that can talk to PHP-FPM via FastCGI.

  • The document root is the public/ directory of the installation, for example /var/www/userli/public.
  • All requests that don't match a file have to be passed to public/index.php.
  • Always use HTTPS.

The examples below are starting points. Adjust paths, PHP-FPM socket and TLS to your system.

docs.title: Caddy
docs.text:
Caddy obtains TLS certificates automatically.

users.example.org {
    root * /var/www/userli/public
    encode gzip
    php_fastcgi unix//run/php/php8.4-fpm.sock
    file_server
}

docs.title: Nginx
docs.text:
server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    http2 on;
    server_name users.example.org;

    ssl_certificate     /etc/letsencrypt/live/users.example.org/fullchain.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/users.example.org/privkey.pem;

    root /var/www/userli/public;

    location / {
        try_files $uri /index.php$is_args$args;
    }

    location ~ ^/index\.php(/|$) {
        fastcgi_pass unix:/run/php/php8.4-fpm.sock;
        fastcgi_split_path_info ^(.+\.php)(/.*)$;
        include fastcgi_params;
        fastcgi_param SCRIPT_FILENAME $realpath_root$fastcgi_script_name;
        fastcgi_param DOCUMENT_ROOT $realpath_root;
        internal;
    }

    # Deny access to all other PHP files
    location ~ \.php$ {
        return 404;
    }
}

server {
    listen 80;
    server_name users.example.org;
    return 301 https://$host$request_uri;
}

docs.title: Apache
docs.text:
Requires mod_rewrite, mod_ssl, mod_headers and mod_proxy_fcgi.

<VirtualHost *:80>
    ServerName users.example.org
    Redirect permanent / https://users.example.org/
</VirtualHost>

<VirtualHost *:443>
    ServerName users.example.org
    DocumentRoot /var/www/userli/public

    <Directory /var/www/userli/public>
        AllowOverride None
        Require all granted
        FallbackResource /index.php
    </Directory>

    <FilesMatch \.php$>
        SetHandler "proxy:unix:/run/php/php8.4-fpm.sock|fcgi://localhost"
    </FilesMatch>

    Protocols h2 http/1.1
    SSLEngine On
    SSLCertificateFile    /etc/letsencrypt/live/users.example.org/fullchain.pem
    SSLCertificateKeyFile /etc/letsencrypt/live/users.example.org/privkey.pem

    Header always set Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"
</VirtualHost>

docs.title: Additional hostnames
docs.text:
• Web Key Directory: If the domains of your users don't point to Userli, forward /.well-known/openpgpkey/ from those hosts to Userli. See Web Key Directory.
  • MTA-STS: mta-sts.<domain> of every mail domain has to reach Userli. See MTA-STS.

docs.title: Security headers
docs.text:
Userli sets a Content Security Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy itself. You only need to add Strict-Transport-Security in the webserver.

If Userli runs behind a reverse proxy, configure trusted proxies.

docs.title: Web Key Directory
docs.text:
Userli brings support for OpenPGP Web Key Directory, a OpenPGP key discovery system. Users can import and update their OpenPGP key and it will be published in the Web Key Directory according to the OpenPGP Web Key Directory Internet Draft.

Importing OpenPGP keys requires GnuPG (version 2.1.14 or newer) to be installed, as the pear/crypt_gpg library uses it to parse and validate uploaded keys.

Users publish their key in Account settings → OpenPGP Keys, either by uploading a file or by pasting the key as text. The key can be published for the account and for each custom alias. See User Guide → OpenPGP keys.

Admins can list all published keys in Admin → OpenPGP Keys.

Userli serves WKD keys directly via HTTP using the Advanced method. The following routes are provided:

  • /.well-known/openpgpkey/{domain}/hu/{hash} — returns the binary OpenPGP key for the given WKD hash
  • /.well-known/openpgpkey/{domain}/policy — returns an empty policy file

Key lookups are cached with a 24-hour TTL (in Redis if REDIS_URL is configured, otherwise on the filesystem) and automatically invalidated when keys are created, updated, or deleted.

docs.title: DNS and hostnames
docs.text:
WKD clients look up keys of user@example.org in this order:

  1. Advanced method: https://openpgpkey.example.org/.well-known/openpgpkey/example.org/hu/<hash>
  2. Direct method: https://example.org/.well-known/openpgpkey/hu/<hash>

Userli implements the advanced method. For each mail domain, point openpgpkey.<domain> to Userli and include it in the TLS certificate:

openpgpkey.example.org.  IN CNAME  users.example.org.

docs.title: Reverse Proxy Setup
docs.text: If openpgpkey.<domain> is served by another webserver or reverse proxy, forward requests to /.well-known/openpgpkey/ to Userli. Replace upstream and localhost:8000 with the address of your Userli webserver.

docs.title: Nginx
docs.text:
location /.well-known/openpgpkey/ {
    proxy_pass http://upstream;
}

docs.title: Apache 2
docs.text:
ProxyPass "/.well-known/openpgpkey/" "http://localhost:8000/.well-known/openpgpkey/"
ProxyPassReverse "/.well-known/openpgpkey/" "http://localhost:8000/.well-known/openpgpkey/"

docs.title: Caddy
docs.text:
handle /.well-known/openpgpkey/* {
    reverse_proxy localhost:8000
}

docs.title: Mail server integration
docs.text:
Userli doesn't need access to the mail server, and the mail server doesn't need access to the Userli database. All communication goes through authenticated HTTP APIs: the mail server asks Userli, Userli answers.

Service Integration API scope Required Dovecot Lua adapter shipped with Userli dovecot yes, for IMAP/POP3 Postfix userli-postfix-adapter postfix yes, for SMTP Roundcube Roundcube plugin roundcube optional Keycloak Keycloak user provider keycloak optional Other services Retention API retention optional Other services Webhooks – optional Dovecot (mailbox cleanup) userli-mailbox-janitor retention optional

docs.title: API tokens
docs.text:
Every integration authenticates with an API token. Each token has one or more scopes that define which API it may use. Create tokens in the admin interface under Admin → API Tokens (see Admin Guide → API tokens) or on the command line:

# Create a token for Dovecot
bin/console app:api-token:create --name "Dovecot mx1" --scopes dovecot

# Create a token with several scopes
bin/console app:api-token:create --name "Mail host" --scopes dovecot --scopes postfix

# Delete a token
bin/console app:api-token:delete --token <PLAIN_TOKEN>

Send the token with each request:

Authorization: Bearer <PLAIN_TOKEN>

X-API-Token: <PLAIN_TOKEN> is accepted as a fallback.

  • Tokens are stored hashed; the plain token is shown only once.
  • A token without the required scope gets HTTP 403.
  • The last use of each token is shown in the admin interface.

Use one token per service and host with only the scopes it needs. All API endpoints are listed in the API reference.

docs.title: Account status and the mail server
docs.text:
The APIs enforce the account status, so the mail server doesn't need its own logic:

Account state IMAP/POP3 login (Dovecot) SMTP auth (Postfix) Incoming mail active ✓ ✓ ✓ password change required ✗ ✗ ✓ role Spam ✗ ✗ ✓ deleted ✗ ✗ ✗

Replaced by scoped API tokens

The settings DOVECOT_API_*, KEYCLOAK_API_* and RETENTION_API_* (enable flags, IP allowlists and access tokens) have been removed. Use scoped API tokens instead.

docs.title: Dovecot
docs.text:
Dovecot asks Userli to authenticate IMAP/POP3 users (passdb) and to look up mailbox details (userdb): quota and – if MailCrypt is enabled – the encryption keys.

The connection is made by a Lua script, the Userli Dovecot adapter. It is released as a separate tarball with every Userli release (userli-dovecot-adapter-x.y.z.tar.gz). The adapter is only guaranteed to be compatible with the same Userli version and requires Dovecot 2.4.

sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Mail client
    participant D as Dovecot
    participant U as Userli
    C->>D: IMAP LOGIN user@example.org password
    D->>U: POST /api/dovecot/user@example.org {password}
    U-->>D: 200 + MailCrypt keys (decrypted with password)
    D->>U: GET /api/dovecot/user@example.org
    U-->>D: 200 quota, MailCrypt public key
    D-->>C: OK

docs.title: On the Userli host
docs.text:
Create an API token with the scope dovecot:

  • in the admin interface under Admin → API Tokens, or

  • on the command line:

    bin/console app:api-token:create --name "Dovecot" --scopes dovecot

docs.title: Install Lua dependencies
docs.text:
On Debian based systems, run

sudo apt update
sudo apt install lua5.4 lua-json dovecot-auth-lua

docs.title: Install the adapter
docs.text:
Install the adapter script to a suitable location, like /usr/local/bin/:

cd /usr/local/bin/
wget https://github.com/systemli/userli/releases/download/x.y.z/userli-dovecot-adapter-x.y.z.tar.gz
# Check signature and hash sum, see "Install from release"
tar -xvzf userli-dovecot-adapter-x.y.z.tar.gz

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Default Description USERLI_API_ACCESS_TOKEN – Required. Plain API token with the dovecot scope. USERLI_HOST – Required. Host (and optional port) of Userli, without scheme and path, e.g. users.example.org. DOVECOT_LUA_INSECURE false Use plain HTTP instead of HTTPS. Only for local testing. DOVECOT_LUA_MAX_ATTEMPTS 3 Number of attempts per request. DOVECOT_LUA_TIMEOUT 10000 Timeout per request in milliseconds. DOVECOT_LUA_AGENT Userli-Dovecot-Adapter HTTP user agent.

Set them in the environment of the Dovecot service, for example with a systemd drop-in:

/etc/systemd/system/dovecot.service.d/userli.conf
[Service]
Environment=USERLI_HOST=users.example.org
Environment=USERLI_API_ACCESS_TOKEN=<PLAIN_TOKEN>

docs.title: Authentication
Mail location
docs.text:
Store mails in a separate directory per user, for example:

/etc/dovecot/conf.d/10-mail.conf
mail_home = /srv/vmail/%{user|domain}/%{user|username}
mail_driver = maildir
mail_path = ~/Maildir
mail_uid = vmail
mail_gid = vmail

docs.title: MailCrypt
docs.text:
To enable mailbox encryption, enable the mail_crypt plugin, but disable encryption by default:

/etc/dovecot/conf.d/90-mail-crypt.conf
mail_plugins {
    mail_crypt = yes
}

crypt_write_algorithm =

The empty crypt_write_algorithm disables encryption by default. This is necessary to not break incoming mail for users without MailCrypt keys. The adapter sets the algorithm and the keys for every user with MailCrypt enabled.

docs.title: Test
docs.text:
doveadm auth test user@example.org
doveadm user user@example.org

See the Dovecot documentation on Lua authentication and debugging authentication.

docs.title: Keycloak
docs.text:
With the Keycloak User Provider for Userli, Keycloak uses Userli accounts for single sign-on. Users can then sign in to other services (for example Nextcloud, Matrix or a wiki) with their email address and password – and their Userli 2FA code.

The provider uses the /api/keycloak/ endpoints to search users, count them and validate passwords and TOTP codes. Keycloak doesn't store passwords.

docs.title: On the Userli host
docs.text:
Create an API token with the scope keycloak:

bin/console app:api-token:create --name "Keycloak" --scopes keycloak

docs.title: In Keycloak
docs.text: Install the provider and add it as a user federation provider in your realm. Configure the Userli URL, the domain and the API token. See the provider README and Keycloak's documentation on user storage providers.

docs.title: Account status
docs.text:
Credential validation enforces the account status like the Dovecot API:

State HTTP message Authenticated 200 success Unknown user or bad credentials 403 authentication failed Deleted or role Spam 403 authentication failed Password change required 403 password change required OTP requested but not enrolled 403 not supported Unknown credential type 400 not supported

Each successful validation updates the last login time of the user, so active Keycloak users are not removed as inactive.

All endpoints are listed in the API reference.

docs.title: Mailbox janitor
docs.text:
Userli has no access to the mailboxes on the mail server and therefore doesn't delete or reset them. The userli-mailbox-janitor is a small Go service running on the Dovecot host that does this for you:

  • Delete mailboxes of deleted users after a retention period (user.deleted webhook).
  • Purge mailboxes of reset users immediately (user.reset webhook). After a reset, old emails can't be decrypted anymore, so they are removed.
  • Keep forwarding-only accounts alive: users whose Sieve script redirects all mail never sign in. The janitor reports them as active via the Retention API, so they aren't removed as inactive.
flowchart LR
    U[Userli] -->|webhook POST /userli| J[userli-mailbox-janitor]
    J -->|HTTPS /api/retention| U
    J -->|purge command| M[(Mailboxes)]
    J -->|read| S[(Sieve scripts)]

docs.title: On the Userli host
docs.text:
Create an API token with the scope retention:

bin/console app:api-token:create --name "Mailbox janitor mx1" --scopes retention

Create a webhook endpoint in Admin → Webhooks (see Admin Guide → Webhooks):

  • URL: https://<janitor-host>/userli
  • Events: user.deleted and user.reset
  • Secret: a random string, used as WEBHOOK_SECRET below

docs.title: On the mail server
docs.text:
Download a binary for your platform from the releases or build it from source:

git clone https://github.com/systemli/userli-mailbox-janitor.git
cd userli-mailbox-janitor
go build -o userli-mailbox-janitor

Configure it with environment variables and run it as a service, for example with systemd as the vmail user:

WEBHOOK_SECRET=<WEBHOOK_SECRET>
USERLI_URL=https://userli.example.org
USERLI_TOKEN=<PLAIN_TOKEN>
PURGER_DATABASE_PATH=/var/lib/userli-mailbox-janitor/mailboxes.csv
PURGER_COMMAND="rm -rf /var/vmail/{domain}/{local_part}"
TOUCHER_SIEVE_LOCATION=/var/vmail/{domain}/{local_part}/.dovecot.sieve
Variable Default Description WEBHOOK_SECRET – (required) Secret of the webhook endpoint in Userli. USERLI_URL – (required) Base URL of Userli. USERLI_TOKEN – (required) API token with the scope retention. TOUCHER_SIEVE_LOCATION – (required) Path to the Sieve script of a user. Supports {domain} and {local_part}. TOUCHER_USE_SUDO false Read Sieve scripts with sudo. TOUCHER_TICK_INTERVAL 24h How often inactive users are checked. PURGER_COMMAND echo … (does nothing) Command that deletes a mailbox. Supports {email}, {domain} and {local_part}. PURGER_RETENTION_HOURS 24 Hours between deletion and purging the mailbox. PURGER_TICK_INTERVAL 1h How often due mailboxes are purged. PURGER_DATABASE_PATH ./mailboxes.csv File storing pending deletions. LISTEN_ADDR :8080 HTTP listen address. LOG_LEVEL info debug, info, warn or error.

GET /health returns 200 OK and can be used for monitoring.

Warning

PURGER_COMMAND runs via /bin/sh and permanently deletes data. Test it with a dummy account before going live. The janitor serves plain HTTP – put a reverse proxy with HTTPS in front of it if Userli runs on another host.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Deleted users: each user.deleted event is appended to the CSV file (PURGER_DATABASE_PATH) with a timestamp. Once PURGER_RETENTION_HOURS have passed, the janitor runs PURGER_COMMAND and removes the entry. Until then, you can cancel a deletion – for example after restoring a user – by removing the line from the file. Failed purges stay in the file and are retried.

Reset users: on a user.reset event, PURGER_COMMAND runs immediately. Dovecot creates a new, empty mailbox at the next login.

Forwarding-only users: every TOUCHER_TICK_INTERVAL, the janitor fetches inactive users from GET /api/retention/users and reads their Sieve script. If it contains an unconditional redirect (if true { redirect … }), the janitor calls PUT /api/retention/<email>/touch.

docs.title: Postfix
docs.text:
Postfix uses Userli to decide

  • which domains and mailboxes exist,
  • where aliases go (including postmaster@ and abuse@),
  • which sender addresses a user may use,
  • how many emails a user may send (SMTP quota),
  • whether an SMTP client may authenticate (SASL).

The connection is made by the userli-postfix-adapter, a small Go service running next to Postfix. It implements the Postfix socketmap protocol, a policy server for rate limiting and a Dovecot-compatible SASL server.

flowchart LR
    P[Postfix] -->|socketmap :10001| A[userli-postfix-adapter]
    P -->|policy :10003| A
    P -->|SASL :10006| A
    A -->|HTTPS /api/postfix| U[Userli]
    A --- R[(Redis)]

docs.title: On the Userli host
docs.text:
Create an API token with the scope postfix:

bin/console app:api-token:create --name "Postfix" --scopes postfix

docs.title: Run the adapter
docs.text:
Install the adapter from its releases or run its container image. It needs Redis for caching and rate limiting. Main settings:

Variable Description USERLI_BASE_URL URL of Userli, e.g. https://users.example.org USERLI_TOKEN API token with the postfix scope REDIS_URL Redis connection, e.g. redis://localhost:6379/0 SASL_LISTEN_ADDR Enables SMTP authentication, e.g. :10006 or /var/spool/postfix/private/auth POSTFIX_RECIPIENT_DELIMITER Your recipient_delimiter, e.g. +

See the adapter README for all options and its metrics.

docs.title: Lookups
docs.text:
/etc/postfix/main.cf
virtual_mailbox_domains = socketmap:inet:localhost:10001:domain
virtual_mailbox_maps    = socketmap:inet:localhost:10001:mailbox
virtual_alias_maps      = socketmap:inet:localhost:10001:alias
smtpd_sender_login_maps = socketmap:inet:localhost:10001:senders

Deliver mail to Dovecot via LMTP, for example virtual_transport = lmtp:unix:private/dovecot-lmtp.

To stop users from sending with addresses that don't belong to them, add reject_sender_login_mismatch to smtpd_sender_restrictions on the submission port.

docs.title: SMTP authentication
docs.text:
/etc/postfix/main.cf
smtpd_sasl_type = dovecot
smtpd_sasl_path = inet:localhost:10006
smtpd_sasl_auth_enable = yes

Authentication fails for deleted accounts, accounts with the role Spam and accounts that have to change their password. You can also use Dovecot's SASL server instead.

docs.title: Rate limiting
docs.text:
/etc/postfix/main.cf
smtpd_end_of_data_restrictions = check_policy_service inet:localhost:10003

The limits come from Userli: per user or alias, or the global default (see Admin Guide → Settings).

docs.title: Test
docs.text:
postmap -q "example.org" socketmap:inet:localhost:10001:domain
postmap -q "user@example.org" socketmap:inet:localhost:10001:mailbox
postmap -q "alias@example.org" socketmap:inet:localhost:10001:alias
postmap -q "user@example.org" socketmap:inet:localhost:10001:senders

Lookups are cached in Userli and in the adapter for a few minutes. Changes may take a short time to reach Postfix.

docs.title: Retention
docs.text:
Userli removes accounts that were not used for about two years (see Maintenance). Every sign-in – web, Dovecot, Postfix, Keycloak – updates the last login time of a user.

Some services issue long-lived sessions or tokens and don't authenticate against Userli regularly. Their users might look inactive although they use the service every day. The Retention API solves this:

  • Touch: report that a user was active in your service.
  • List inactive users: find users without login for two years, for example to clean up their data in your service.

See userli-synapse-user-retention for an example implementation for Matrix Synapse.

docs.title: On the Userli host
docs.text:
Create an API token with the scope retention:

bin/console app:api-token:create --name "Synapse retention" --scopes retention

docs.title: Touch last login
docs.text:
PUT /api/retention/<email>/touch
Authorization: Bearer <PLAIN_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "timestamp": 1693843200 }

timestamp is an optional Unix timestamp of the last activity. It must not be in the future. Without it, the current time is used.

docs.title: List inactive users
docs.text:
GET /api/retention/users
Authorization: Bearer <PLAIN_TOKEN>

Returns the email addresses of users without login for two years.

docs.title: Roundcube
docs.text: The Roundcube Userli plugin creates a Roundcube identity for each alias of a user when they sign in to Roundcube. Users can then send emails from their aliases without setting up identities manually.

docs.title: On the Userli host
docs.text:
Create an API token with the scope roundcube:

bin/console app:api-token:create --name "Roundcube" --scopes roundcube

docs.title: On the Roundcube host
docs.text:
Install the plugin, either with Composer (systemli/userli) or by cloning the repository into the plugins/ directory, and enable it in the Roundcube configuration:

config/config.inc.php
$config['plugins'] = ['userli' /* , ... */];

Configure it in plugins/userli/config.inc.php (copy from config.inc.php.dist):

plugins/userli/config.inc.php
$config['userli_url'] = 'https://users.example.org';
$config['userli_token'] = '<PLAIN_TOKEN>';
$config['userli_ssl_verify'] = true;

docs.title: Webmail link
docs.text: Set the URL of Roundcube as Webmail URL in Admin → Settings to show a Webmail card to users.

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text:
Userli sends webhooks to notify external services about user-related events, for example to create or remove accounts in Nextcloud or Matrix, or to delete the mailbox of a deleted user on the mail server.

Info

We provide a webhook listener to inform Nextcloud and Synapse about user changes. See userli-webhook-listener. To delete and reset mailboxes on a Dovecot server, use the mailbox janitor.

Webhooks are configured by admins in Admin → Webhooks, see Admin Guide → Webhooks. This page describes what a receiver has to implement.

docs.title: Events
docs.text: Event Triggered when user.created A user registered with an invite code. Users created in the admin interface don't trigger this event. user.deleted A user was deleted – by themselves, by an admin, by the CLI or by the removal of inactive users. Not sent when a whole domain is deleted. user.reset An admin set a new password for a user with MailCrypt keys, or app:users:reset was run. Password, MailCrypt keys, recovery token and 2FA were reset; old encrypted emails are unreadable.

docs.title: Domain filtering
docs.text:
Webhook endpoints can optionally be limited to one or more domains.

  • No domains selected (default): the endpoint receives events for users on all domains.
  • One or more domains selected: the endpoint only receives events for users of those domains.

Warning

If a domain is deleted and it was the only domain assigned to a webhook endpoint, that endpoint is automatically disabled to prevent it from silently becoming global.

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
Userli sends a POST request with a JSON body:

{
    "type": "user.deleted",
    "timestamp": "2025-09-10T11:36:14+00:00",
    "data": {
        "email": "user@example.org"
    }
}

Headers:

Header Description Content-Type application/json X-Webhook-Signature HMAC-SHA256 signature of the request body, see Security. X-Webhook-Id Unique identifier of the delivery. X-Webhook-Attempt Number of the attempt, starting at 1.

docs.title: Delivery and retries
docs.text:
• A delivery is successful if your endpoint returns any 2xx status code within 10 seconds (including connection setup).
  • All other status codes, network errors and timeouts are retried up to three times: after 10 seconds, 60 seconds and 6 minutes. After that, the delivery is marked as failed.
  • Admins can retry a delivery manually in the admin interface.
  • Successful deliveries are removed after 14 days, failed ones are kept.

Webhooks are sent by the worker. If it isn't running, no webhooks are sent.

Recommendations for receivers:

  • Validate the signature before processing.
  • Respond quickly. Offload slow work to a queue and return 2xx once the event is stored.
  • Make processing idempotent. Use X-Webhook-Id to detect duplicates.
  • Alert if many events need more than one attempt.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Each request is signed with the secret configured for the endpoint:

X-Webhook-Signature = hex(hmac_sha256(secret, body))

Compute the signature over the raw request body and compare it in constant time. Example in Python:

import hashlib
import hmac

def is_valid(secret: str, body: bytes, signature: str) -> bool:
    expected = hmac.new(secret.encode(), body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature)

Only accept webhooks via HTTPS.

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text:
This guide is for people who have an email account on a service that runs Userli – or who want to get one. You don't need any technical knowledge.

Names and addresses differ

Userli is used by different email providers. Your provider may use its own name and web address instead of "Userli". Menus and buttons are the same. In this guide, example.org stands for the domain of your provider.

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text: I want to … Read get a new email account Create an account sign in, change my password or language Sign in and your account protect my account with a second factor Secure your account get back into my account after losing my password Forgot your password use extra addresses that forward to my inbox Aliases invite a friend Invite codes let others find my OpenPGP key automatically OpenPGP keys delete my account Delete your account

docs.title: Reading and writing emails
docs.text:
Userli manages your account, but it is not an email program. To read and write emails, either

  • use the Webmail of your provider (if available, there is a Webmail card on your account overview), or
  • set up an email program such as Thunderbird, K-9 Mail or the mail app on your phone. Ask your provider for the server settings (IMAP and SMTP server names and ports). Use your full email address as username and your Userli password.

docs.title: Your privacy and security in short
docs.text:
• Choose a strong, unique password. It must have at least 12 characters and must not appear in known data breaches.
  • Store your recovery token in a safe place. It is the only way back into your account if you forget your password – your provider cannot reset it for you without losing your encrypted emails.
  • Turn on two-factor authentication to protect your account even if your password gets stolen.

docs.title: Need help?
docs.text: If something does not work as described, contact the support of your email provider. If you are locked out after a spam warning, only your provider can unlock your account.

docs.title: Sign in
docs.text:
Open the web address of your provider and click Sign in (or use the form on the start page). Enter

  • E-mail: your full email address. On most services, the part before the @ is enough for addresses on the main domain.
  • Password: your password.

If you have turned on two-factor authentication, you are asked for a 6-digit code afterwards.

If the sign-in fails, check your address and password. Forgot your password? Click Password forgotten? and follow Forgot your password.

To sign out, open the user menu at the top right and click Log out.

docs.title: Your account overview
docs.text:
After signing in you see the overview of your account:

Card What it does Webmail Opens the webmail of your provider (only shown if available). Invite codes Shows your invite codes (only shown if invitations are enabled). Alias addresses Manage your aliases. Account settings Password, two-factor authentication, recovery token, app passwords, OpenPGP keys and account deletion.

docs.title: Security alert
docs.text: If your password was found in a database of known data breaches, a red Security Alert banner appears on every page. Your password is checked automatically when you sign in. Change your password as soon as possible – the banner disappears afterwards.

docs.title: Account locked
docs.text: If you see the page "Account locked", your provider believes that a spammer has misused your account and has turned off email access. Contact the support of your provider to unlock it.

docs.title: Account settings
docs.text: Account → Account settings shows the status of your security features at a glance.

docs.title: Change your password
docs.text:
Go to Account settings → Password. Enter your current password and your new password twice, then click Submit.

The new password must have at least 12 characters, must not appear in known data breaches and must differ from the old one.

Tip

Changing your password does not change your recovery token. Your existing token stays valid.

Password change required

If your admin requires a password change (for example, after setting an initial password for you), every page redirects to the password form until you have chosen a new password. Your email program cannot sign in until then, either.

docs.title: Change the language
docs.text:
Open the user menu at the top right and choose a Language. Userli also uses the language of your web browser automatically. Emails from Userli are sent in the language you are using.

You can switch between light and dark mode with the toggle in the navigation bar.

docs.title: Aliases
docs.text:
An alias is an additional email address. Emails to an alias arrive in your normal inbox. Aliases help you to keep your main address private and to see who passed on your address.

Go to Aliases in the navigation. All aliases use the same domain as your account.

docs.title: Custom aliases
docs.text:
Custom aliases have a name you choose, for example newsletter@example.org.

  • You can create up to 3 custom aliases.
  • Allowed are lowercase letters, digits and -, _ and ..
  • The name must not be in use or reserved.
  • Custom aliases can't be deleted by you. Choose carefully. If you need one removed, contact your provider.

To create one, enter the name under Create new custom alias and click Add.

docs.title: Random aliases
docs.text:
Random aliases have a generated name of 24 letters and digits, for example k3j9x0q2m7...@example.org. They are ideal for online shops, newsletters and sign-ups.

  • You can have up to 100 random aliases.
  • Add an optional note (up to 40 characters) to remember what you used the alias for.
  • Delete a random alias at any time with Delete alias. After that, emails to this address are no longer delivered. A deleted address can't be used again.

To create one, optionally enter a note and click Generate random alias address.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• You receive an email whenever a new alias is created for your account.
  • To send emails from an alias, set it up as an additional identity in your email program or webmail. Most providers allow sending from your own aliases.
  • To let others find your OpenPGP key for a custom alias, see OpenPGP keys.

docs.title: App passwords
docs.text:
An app password is a separate password for one email program, for example Thunderbird on your laptop or the mail app on your phone. Use it instead of your password when you set up the app.

App passwords work for reading and sending email (IMAP, SMTP) in mail programs like Thunderbird or Apple Mail. They do not work for signing in to this web interface or to other services.

This makes them safer than using your password everywhere:

  • Someone who finds out an app password can only read and send your email. They can't sign in here, so they can't change your password or take over your account.
  • If a device gets lost, delete its app password. Your password and your other devices keep working.

docs.title: Generate an app password
docs.text:
1. Go to Account settings → App Passwords.
  2. Enter a Name that tells you where you use it, for example Thunderbird on laptop. Each name can be used only once.
  3. Enter your current password to confirm it's you and click Generate app password.
  4. Copy the new app password and enter it in your email program instead of your password.

Warning

The app password is shown only once. If you lose it, delete it and create a new one.

docs.title: Delete an app password
docs.text:
The list shows roughly when each app password was last used, for example last week or 3 months ago. Delete the ones you no longer need.

Go to Account settings → App Passwords, click the delete button (×) next to the app password and confirm. The app using it can't sign in anymore.

Changing your password does not delete your app passwords. If you reset your password with your recovery token, your provider resets your account or you delete your account, all app passwords are deleted.

docs.title: Delete your account
docs.text:
Before you delete

Save the emails you want to keep, for example by copying them to a local folder in your email program. After deletion you can't sign in anymore.

Go to Account settings and click Delete Account. In the dialog, enter your password and click Delete account. You are signed out immediately and can't sign in to the web interface or your email program anymore. Your provider usually removes the mailbox with your emails from the mail server after a while.

Deletion cannot be undone

  • Your password, app passwords, recovery token and mailbox encryption keys are deleted. Your encrypted emails can't be decrypted anymore.
  • All your aliases are deleted.
  • Unused invite codes are deleted.
  • Your address can never be registered again – not by you, not by anybody else.

docs.title: Inactive accounts
docs.text: Your provider may delete accounts that were not used for about two years. Signing in to the web interface or your email program counts as use.

docs.title: Invite codes
docs.text: New accounts can only be created with an invite code. As a user, you can receive invite codes to invite your friends.

docs.title: When do I get invite codes?
docs.text:
Your provider decides per domain whether invitations are possible, how many invite codes each user gets and how long the waiting period is. By default, users get 3 invite codes 7 days after registration.

You get your invite codes when

  • invitations are enabled for your domain,
  • your account is older than the waiting period, and
  • you have signed in at least once.

Open Invite codes in the navigation to see them. If you still have to wait, the page shows the date when you get your codes. The number is a total – used codes are not replaced.

If the menu entry is missing, invitations are disabled for your domain or your account is not allowed to invite others.

docs.title: Invite a friend
docs.text:
Click Copy to clipboard next to an unused code. This copies a complete registration link like https://users.example.org/register/aB3xY9. Send it to your friend. They can open it and create an account.

Each code can be used once. Used codes show the date they were redeemed.

Invite people you trust

You are responsible for the people you invite. If accounts are misused for spam, your provider may also block the invite codes of the person who invited them.

docs.title: OpenPGP keys
docs.text:
OpenPGP lets people encrypt emails so that only the recipient can read them. To send you an encrypted email, others need your public key.

If you upload your public key to Userli, it is published in the Web Key Directory (WKD) of your provider. Email programs such as Thunderbird, GnuPG or K-9 Mail with OpenKeychain then find your key automatically when someone writes to you.

Note

Only upload your public key. Never share your private key.

docs.title: Publish a key
docs.text:
1. Go to Account settings → OpenPGP Keys.
  2. Find the address – your own address or one of your custom aliases – and click Upload.
  3. Either choose your key file (up to 4 MB) or paste the key as text (it starts with -----BEGIN PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----).
  4. Click Publish OpenPGP key.

The uploaded data must contain exactly one key for that address. Afterwards the card shows the key ID, the fingerprint and the expiry date.

To export your public key with GnuPG:

gpg --export --armor you@example.org > publickey.asc

docs.title: Replace or delete a key
docs.text:
• Replace: click Replace and upload the new key, for example after extending its expiry date.
  • Delete: click Delete, enter your password and confirm. The key is removed from the Web Key Directory.

Keys can be published for your own address and for custom aliases, not for random aliases.

docs.title: Forgot your password
docs.text:
If you forgot your password, you can set a new one with your recovery token. Your emails stay readable.

Without a recovery token

If you have lost both your password and your recovery token, only your provider can help. An admin can set a new password, but your existing encrypted emails will be lost.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
For your security, password recovery takes two steps with a waiting period of 48 hours in between. During this time, you receive an email and can stop the recovery in case someone else started it.

flowchart LR
    A[Enter address<br/>and recovery token] --> B[Wait 48 hours]
    B --> C[Enter address and<br/>recovery token again]
    C --> D[Set new password]
    D --> E[Store new<br/>recovery token]

docs.title: Step 1: Start the recovery
docs.text:
1. Click Password forgotten? on the sign-in page.
  2. Enter your E-mail address and your Recovery token and click Recover.
  3. The page shows the date and time when you can continue. Keep your recovery token until then.

You receive an email that your password will be reset. The waiting period can't be shortened.

You didn't start this?

If you receive this email but did not start the recovery, someone else knows your recovery token. Sign in and create a new recovery token immediately. This stops the recovery.

docs.title: Step 2: Set a new password
docs.text:
After 48 hours, open Password forgotten? again and enter the same address and recovery token. Now you can choose a new password (at least 12 characters, not found in known data breaches).

You have 30 days to finish this step. After that, you have to start again.

docs.title: Step 3: Store your new recovery token
docs.text:
Your old recovery token has been used up. Userli shows you a new recovery token. Store it safely, confirm and click Continue. Then sign in with your new password.

Two-factor authentication and app passwords are reset

The recovery turns off two-factor authentication, because you may have lost your phone as well. Turn it on again after signing in.

It also deletes all app passwords, in case someone else created one. Create new ones for your mail apps.

docs.title: Create an account
docs.text:
New accounts can only be created with an invite code. An invite code is a code of six letters and digits, for example aB3xY9. You get one from someone who already has an account – every user can receive invite codes to invite friends (see Invite codes).

Why invite codes?

Invite codes protect the service from mass registrations by spammers. If you don't know anybody with an account, ask your provider whether they give out invite codes.

docs.title: Step 1: Enter the invite code
docs.text:
You can start in two ways:

  • You got a link like https://users.example.org/register/aB3xY9: open it, and you skip directly to step 2.
  • You got only the code: open the start page of your provider, enter it in the Registration box under Invite code and click Create account.

If the code is wrong or was already used, you see "The invite code is invalid." or "The invite code has already been used." If you see the page "Registration closed", your provider has stopped registrations for now.

docs.title: Step 2: Choose your address and password
docs.text:
Your preferred e-mail address : Enter only the part before the @. The domain is fixed by the invite code.

* Use 3 to 32 characters.
* Allowed are lowercase letters, digits and `-`, `_` and `.`.
* Some names such as `admin`, `abuse` or `postmaster` are reserved.
* An address that was used before – even by a deleted account – can never
  be registered again.

Password and Confirm password : Your password must

* have at least 12 characters, and
* not appear in a database of known data breaches
  ([Have I Been Pwned](https://haveibeenpwned.com/Passwords)).

The meter below the field shows whether your password is strong enough.
Use a password that you don't use anywhere else. A password manager helps.

Click Submit.

docs.title: Step 3: Store your recovery token
docs.text:
Right after registration you see your recovery token – a long code like 1a2b3c4d-..... If you forget your password, this token is the only way to get back into your account and keep your emails readable.

  • Copy it with Copy to clipboard and store it somewhere safe, for example in a password manager or printed on paper.
  • The token is shown only once. Nobody, including your provider, can show it to you again.

Check I stored the recovery token at a secure place and click Continue.

docs.title: Step 4: Welcome
docs.text:
Your account is ready and you are signed in. The welcome page suggests the next steps:

  • Set up your email program or open the webmail.
  • Turn on two-factor authentication.
  • Publish your OpenPGP key, if you use one.
  • Invite friends – after a waiting period you get invite codes, too.

You also receive a welcome email in your new inbox.

docs.title: Secure your account
docs.text: Two features protect your account: two-factor authentication keeps others out even if they know your password, and the recovery token lets you back in if you forget your password.

docs.title: Two-factor authentication
docs.text:
With two-factor authentication (2FA) you need a 6-digit code from an authenticator app on your phone, in addition to your password, to sign in to the web interface. The code changes every 30 seconds.

You need an authenticator app (TOTP), for example Aegis (Android), Tofu (iOS) or the app of your password manager.

Note

2FA protects the sign-in to the web interface. Your email program keeps using only your password, or an app password.

docs.title: Turn on 2FA
docs.text:
1. Go to Account settings → Two-Factor Authentication.
  2. Enter your password and click Set up.
  3. Scan the QR code with your authenticator app. If you can't scan it, copy the Setup Key and enter it manually in the app.
  4. Enter the 6-digit code shown in the app under Authentication code and click Verify.
  5. You now see six backup codes. Each backup code can be used once instead of a code from the app – for example, if you lose your phone. Copy them and store them safely, check Backup codes stored securely and click Verify.

2FA is now active.

Warning

The backup codes are shown only once. To get new ones, turn 2FA off and on again.

docs.title: Sign in with 2FA
docs.text: After entering your email address and password, open your authenticator app and enter the current code under Authentication code. Instead of the code you can also enter one of your unused backup codes.

docs.title: Turn off 2FA
docs.text: Go to Account settings → Two-Factor Authentication, enter your password and click Disable.

docs.title: Recovery token
docs.text:
The recovery token is a long code like 1a2b3c4d-5e6f-7a8b-9c0d-1e2f3a4b5c6d. You received it when you created your account. With it you can set a new password if you forget yours.

Your emails are stored encrypted. Only your password – or your recovery token – can unlock them. That is why your provider can't simply reset your password without making your old emails unreadable.

docs.title: Create a new recovery token
docs.text:
Create a new token if you lost the old one, if somebody else might know it, or if your account doesn't have one yet (the card shows Not configured).

  1. Go to Account settings → Recovery Token.
  2. Enter your password and click Create new recovery token.
  3. Copy the new token and store it safely. Check I stored the recovery token at a secure place and click Continue.

The old token stops working immediately. A password recovery that somebody started with the old token is cancelled.
